items.title: South African court sets limits on anti-migrant demonstration
items.description: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside a court in South Africa’s coastal city of Durban on Friday as the government sought judicial intervention to rein in anti-migrant demonstrations that have turned deadly, leaving one person dead last week. Durban, the Zulu heartland, has emerged as a focal point of anti-migrant agitation led by the March and March movement, which has organised demonstrations against undocumented foreigners across the country for months. Some demonstrations have turned violent, including last week when a mob of about 50 people beat a foreign national to death, prompting President Cyril Ramaphosa to deploy more than 500 soldiers to support the police. Protesters sang and chanted outside the high court, waving placards reading “reclaim our country” and sticks as police officers kept a close watch. Supporters of several political parties, including the centre-right ActionSA and the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party led by former president Jacob Zuma, also turned out in solidarity. Judge Peter Olsen allowed March and March movement to proceed with its planned demonstrations, but under tighter conditions following amendments to the government’s application. Under the revised terms, the group may march between 9am and 3pm, with participants barred from carrying weapons or covering their faces. The group was also prohibited from destroying property or setting fire to buildings. The matter is expected to return to court next year. The court action was brought by acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia, who was seeking to stop the demonstrations on the grounds that they threaten public order and the safety of foreign nationals. He cited police intelligence about an alleged plot to set fire to the Home Affairs Refugee Reception Centre in Berea, an inner-city suburb of Durban where asylum seekers go to seek documentation. The unrest has been fuelled by misinformation about a July Constitutional Court ruling that asylum seekers cannot be denied access to South Africa’s asylum system solely on procedural grounds, according to the police. – ‘Widespread violence’ – Counsel for the police told the court on Friday that the situation in Durban had “degenerated into lawlessness” that reactive policing could no longer contain. More than 400 police officers had been deployed, but this had “proved structurally unable to stem the widespread violence”, they said. March and March defended its right to demonstrate under the constitution, distancing itself from the violence and insisting it should not be held responsible for the actions of those involved. “The agenda is to try and silence the people,” March and March legal representative Xolani Zuma told reporters ahead of the court decision. “The real problem are illegal immigrants who are here in the country and terrorising people,” he said. The court battle comes days before local elections on November 4, with lawyers warning that police are already stretched thin ahead of the vote. Populist groups leading the demonstrations accuse migrants of taking jobs and public services from South Africans, an issue that has become a flashpoint ahead of the polls. At least five foreign nationals have been killed in anti-migrant violence this year, according to police, although some African governments have put the toll higher. Police said the nationality of last week’s victim was still under investigation. The post South African court sets limits on anti-migrant demonstration appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SIAO 2026 : Le Ghana plaide pour une coopération économique renforcée avec le Burkina Faso
items.description: À l’ouverture de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026, le Ghana, pays invité d’honneur, à travers sa ministre du Commerce, de l’Agroalimentaire et de l’Industrie, Elisabeth Ofosu-Adjare, a réaffirmé sa volonté de renforcer ses relations commerciales avec le Burkina Faso. La cheffe de la délégation ghanéenne a plaidé pour un accord bilatéral sur le commerce et l’investissement, fondé sur la complémentarité des économies des deux pays. La capitale burkinabè accueille, depuis la matinée de ce vendredi 30 octobre, la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Présent à cette cérémonie d’ouverture, le Ghana, pays invité d’honneur, a salué le rayonnement de cette manifestation et exprimé sa reconnaissance aux autorités burkinabè pour cette marque de confiance. Porteuse des salutations fraternelles du président ghanéen, John Dramani Mahama, au président du Faso, Ibrahim Traoré, la ministre Elisabeth Ofosu-Adjare a insisté sur les liens historiques, culturels et économiques qui unissent les deux peuples. « Nous sommes un même peuple », a-t-elle déclaré, évoquant les communautés transfrontalières, les langues partagées, les échanges commerciaux et les liens matrimoniaux qui rapprochent les populations du Burkina Faso et du Ghana depuis des générations, selon elle. Pour la représentante ghanéenne, l’artisanat africain ne doit plus être considéré comme une activité essentiellement traditionnelle. Il doit constituer un véritable levier de développement économique, de création d’emplois et d’affirmation de l’identité culturelle du continent. À cet effet, elle a rappelé que l’initiative Artisanat 84, lancée sous le leadership du président Thomas Sankara, avait permis de réunir des artisans venus des différentes provinces du Burkina Faso. Cette dynamique a ensuite évolué pour donner naissance, en 1988, à la Foire internationale de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou. « Près de quatre décennies plus tard, le SIAO poursuit cette ambition avec des objectifs importants : plus de 6 000 exposants provenant d’une trentaine de pays et près de 800 000 visiteurs attendus », a fait savoir Elisabeth Ofosu-Adjare. Le SIAO 2026 s'est ouvert ce matin À l’échelle mondiale, le marché de l’artisanat représentait environ 740 milliards de dollars en 2024 et pourrait atteindre 1 000 milliards de dollars d’ici à 2030. Pour la ministre ghanéenne chargée de l’Industrie, ces perspectives illustrent les possibilités économiques offertes par un secteur qui demeure encore insuffisamment structuré dans plusieurs pays africains. Elle a ainsi appelé à une meilleure articulation entre les entreprises, les institutions de recherche, les établissements financiers et les autorités de régulation, afin de faciliter la transformation des créations artisanales en produits compétitifs sur les marchés internationaux. Au-delà de la promotion de l’artisanat, Accra entend consolider les échanges commerciaux avec Ouagadougou. La représentante ghanéenne a souligné la complémentarité des deux économies, estimant que celle-ci constitue un atout pour développer des partenariats durables. Le Ghana approvisionne notamment le Burkina Faso en produits plastiques, articles ménagers, fer, acier, engrais, ciment, produits pharmaceutiques, papier et emballages, ainsi qu’en intrants destinés à l’industrie minière. En retour, le Burkina Faso exporte vers le marché ghanéen du bétail, des oignons, de la tomate, du sésame, du beurre de karité, des mangues et d’autres produits agricoles. Dans cette perspective, le Ghana s’est déclaré disposé à conclure un accord bilatéral sur le commerce et l’investissement avec le Burkina Faso, dans le respect des engagements des deux pays au titre de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf). Selon Elisabeth Ofosu-Adjare, cet accord pourrait notamment favoriser l’harmonisation des normes sanitaires et phytosanitaires, la reconnaissance mutuelle des certificats et une meilleure coordination de la gestion des frontières. L’objectif est de fluidifier la circulation des marchandises entre les deux pays sur le corridor Tema-Ouagadougou. La coopération envisagée concerne également les industries créatives. Le Ghana souhaite encourager les partenariats entre artisans, écoles de design et institutions de recherche, faciliter les échanges de compétences et promouvoir conjointement les produits issus des savoir-faire des deux pays. La transformation locale des matières premières, notamment dans les filières du karité, du cuir et de la poterie, figure aussi parmi les pistes de coopération évoquées. Des partenariats dans les chaînes de valeur de la tomate et de la volaille sont également envisagés. Lire aussi : Burkina : C’est parti pour le SIAO 2026 ! Toujours selon Elisabeth Ofosu-Adjare, le Ghana entend, à travers sa participation au SIAO 2026, valoriser la diversité et la qualité de son patrimoine artisanal. Sa délégation, composée de responsables gouvernementaux, d’artisans et d’entrepreneurs issus de ses seize régions, présente notamment des étoffes kente, des créations inspirées des symboles Adinkra, des smocks du Nord, ainsi que des produits artisanaux de Bolgatanga et des créations de mode contemporaines. Ce faisant, elle a invité les visiteurs à découvrir ces produits et à nouer des relations d’affaires avec les exposants. Elle a également annoncé la Journée du Ghana, prévue le mardi 3 novembre 2026, qui sera consacrée à la promotion de la culture et du savoir-faire de son pays. S’adressant aux artisans présents à Ouagadougou, elle les a encouragés à valoriser leurs créations, à défendre leur savoir-faire et à fixer leurs prix avec assurance. Selon elle, l’authenticité, la durabilité et la profondeur culturelle sont désormais des critères recherchés par les consommateurs internationaux. Pour terminer, la représentante du Ghana a salué l’engagement des autorités burkinabè, du comité national d’organisation et des volontaires mobilisés pour la tenue du SIAO. Elle a souhaité une édition fructueuse aux exposants et réaffirmé son attachement à l’amitié entre les deux pays. En somme, le SIAO 2026 constitue une occasion de rapprocher les peuples, de stimuler les échanges et de faire du savoir-faire local un moteur de développement économique. Jean-François SOMÉ Minute.bf

items.title: Mali : des chauffeurs routiers marocains pris au piège de violents affrontements armés
items.description: Des chauffeurs routiers marocains ont échappé de peu à des tirs lors de violents affrontements armés sur plusieurs axes routiers au Mali. Alors que certains se retrouvent bloqués dans la région de Didiéni, les professionnels du transport international appellent leurs confrères à éviter ce corridor devenu particulièrement dangereux. La situation sécuritaire au Mali suscite de vives inquiétudes chez les professionnels marocains du transport international. Jeudi 29 octobre, plusieurs camions marocains transportant des marchandises ont été pris dans des échanges de tirs impliquant des groupes armés et les forces de l'armée malienne. Selon des témoignages recueillis par le média Hespress, les chauffeurs ont échappé à l'attaque sans faire état de victimes, avant de bénéficier d'une protection militaire pour quitter la zone des affrontements. L'incident a relancé les appels à la prudence au sein du secteur du transport routier, alors que plusieurs professionnels continuent d’emprunter les routes maliennes malgré les avertissements répétés concernant la dégradation de la situation sécuritaire. Les témoignages rapportés font état de scènes particulièrement éprouvantes. Pris sous les tirs, certains chauffeurs auraient été contraints de se réfugier sous les structures métalliques de leurs poids lourds pour se protéger des balles. La violence des affrontements aurait notamment touché les axes reliant Nioro à Diéma, ainsi que Nioro à Didiéni. Des itinéraires désormais considérés comme particulièrement risqués par les professionnels du secteur. La situation reste préoccupante pour plusieurs conducteurs. Certains seraient actuellement bloqués dans la région de Didiéni, dans l'impossibilité de poursuivre leur trajet ou de faire demi-tour en raison des tensions sur le terrain. D'autres chauffeurs ont, de leur côté, décidé de rebrousser chemin depuis Nioro en direction de Gogui, afin d'éviter de se retrouver pris au piège des affrontements. Ils affirment attendre une évolution de la situation avant d'envisager tout nouveau déplacement. Selon les témoignages recueillis, les attaques ne viseraient plus uniquement les véhicules de transport de marchandises. Les tirs seraient désormais dirigés directement vers les cabines des camions étrangers, exposant les conducteurs à un danger immédiat. Face à cette situation, l'Union générale des professionnels du transport international et national au Maroc tire la sonnette d'alarme. Son président, Cherki El Hachimi, affirme que les chauffeurs et les propriétaires de camions avaient été alertés à plusieurs reprises sur les risques liés aux déplacements vers le Mali. Ces avertissements auraient notamment été diffusés quotidiennement à travers des groupes WhatsApp et différents médias. Le responsable déplore néanmoins que certains professionnels aient continué à emprunter ces itinéraires malgré les mises en garde. Pour l'organisation, la poursuite des déplacements dans ces conditions expose inutilement les conducteurs à des risques majeurs, mais également leurs marchandises et leurs véhicules. L'Union appelle ainsi le ministère de tutelle à intervenir en urgence et à envisager une suspension temporaire des opérations de transport et d'acheminement de marchandises vers les zones concernées, jusqu'à une stabilisation de la situation sécuritaire et à la mise en place de garanties suffisantes pour protéger les chauffeurs. Alors que les professionnels du secteur redoutent de nouveaux incidents, la situation des conducteurs encore bloqués sur place demeure une source d'inquiétude. Cet épisode remet au premier plan les risques auxquels sont exposés les transporteurs marocains opérant sur certains corridors commerciaux africains, où la dégradation des conditions sécuritaires peut transformer un simple trajet professionnel en véritable épreuve pour leur survie. The post Mali : des chauffeurs routiers marocains pris au piège de violents affrontements armés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Des scientifiques testent la terramation, une alternative écologique à l'inhumation et la crémation
items.description: En France, l'enterrement et la crémation sont aujourd’hui les deux seules pratiques légales. En 2026, près d’un Français sur deux choisit les flammes, séduit par leur prix et leur simplicité. Mais les deux pratiques coûtent et polluent autant. Des chercheurs du CNRS explorent une autre possibilité : la terramation, ou l’art de rendre à la terre ce qu’elle nous a donné. Une expérience inédite menée en région parisienne, qui pourrait bien faire évoluer notre façon d’envisager la mort.

items.title: Clôture du 24e FRATEL à Conakry : Patricia Amand prend les rênes du réseau dans une dynamique d’inclusion et d’innovation numérique
items.description: La 24e Réunion Annuelle du Réseau des régulateurs de télécommunications francophones (FRATEL) s'est achevée à Conakry sur une note d'engagement collectif et de décisions stratégiques pour l'avenir du numérique dans l'espace francophone, a-t-on constaté sur place. Marqué par des échanges denses et une adhésion unanime aux enjeux d'inclusion territoriale, cet événement majeur a consacré l'élection de Patricia Amand, membre du Conseil de Régulation de l'ARTCI (Côte d'Ivoire), à la présidence du FRATEL pour l'année 2027. Un passage de témoin historique et symbolique Succédant à Laure de La Raudière (Présidente de l'Arcep France), première femme à avoir présidé l'organisation, Patricia Amand devient la première Présidente issue du continent africain à prendre la tête du réseau. Dans un discours chaleureux et empreint de reconnaissance, la nouvelle Présidente a salué le leadership de sa prédécesseure ainsi que le rôle charnière joué par Mounir Diawara, ancien membre du Conseil de l'ARTCI, dans la transmission des responsabilités. Elle a également exprimé sa gratitude au ministre Roger Adom, Président du Conseil de Régulation de l'ARTCI depuis mai 2026, pour son soutien institutionnel déterminant, ainsi qu'à l'ensemble des équipes de régulation de la région. Une feuille de route ambitieuse pour 2027 Les travaux de Conakry ont permis de valider des orientations techniques et stratégiques claires pour répondre aux besoins croissants des populations : Décisions publiques fondées sur la donnée : Structuration des choix grâce aux outils de modélisation économique de l'Union Internationale des Télécommunications (UIT). Couverture et aménagement numérique : Intensification du déploiement des réseaux fixes et mobiles pour réduire la fracture numérique territoriale Coordination et régulation renforcées : Harmonisation des actions entre échelons nationaux et locaux, suivi rigoureux des obligations des opérateurs et amélioration des outils de cartographie. Infrastructures du futur : Anticipation des besoins liés à l'intelligence artificielle et au cloud à travers le développement de centres de données (data centers) performants, sécurisés et respectueux de l'environnement. Un appel vibrant à l'action concrète pour l'usager Portant la voix de l'hôte guinéen, Adama Condé, Directeur Général Adjoint de l'ARPT, a lu le discours de clôture de Mamady Doumbouya, Directeur Général de l'ARPT. Rattachant les travaux au programme national visionnaire Simandou 2040, l'ARPT a résumé l'ambition collective en trois piliers vertueux : Mesurer, Partager, Anticipes. « On ne couvre pas ce qu'on ne mesure pas. Personne n'y arrive seul. Les infrastructures de demain se décident aujourd'hui. » En citant symboliquement les figures de citoyens ordinaires Fatoumata à Labé, Sékou à Kankan ou Hawa cherchant du réseau, les dirigeants du FRATEL ont rappelé que chaque décision technique doit se traduire par un accès réel, fiable et accessible au haut débit sur l'ensemble des territoires. Avec l'adoption du rapport d'activité 2026, du plan d'action 2027 et l'entrée du Sénégal (RTP) à la vice-présidence aux côtés de l'équipe de coordination, le FRATEL réaffirme sa position de levier concret pour l'émancipation numérique et l'intégration économique régionale.

items.title: Ghana showcases kente in Moscow as Mahama visits exhibition
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has highlighted cultural understanding as key to Ghana-Russia relations during a visit to a kente exhibition in Moscow. He visited Woven Meanings at the All-Russian Museum of Decorative Arts, an exhibition that brings the artistry and cultural narratives of Ghanaian weaving to Russian audiences. The exhibition presents kente not merely as a traditional fabric but as an expression of Ghanaian history, social values and identity. Its intricate patterns, striking colour combinations and symbolic designs reflect a rich tradition of craftsmanship preserved and transmitted across generations. Among the exhibits are samples of kente and a traditional weaving loom of the type still used by artisans in the Kumasi area. Particularly notable are two kente cloaks: one associated with Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, and the other belonging to President Mahama. The pieces provide a compelling connection between Ghana’s political history and one of its most enduring cultural traditions. For President Mahama, the exhibition represents an important opportunity to deepen understanding between the two countries beyond their formal diplomatic engagements. “Although we have established intergovernmental contacts and relations between our two countries, the strongest and most enduring ties are those between people. And these ties can only be strengthened through an understanding of each other’s cultures,” he observed. He thanked the organisers and their partners for bringing Ghana’s textile heritage to Moscow, particularly acknowledging the interest shown by Russian visitors and the availability of explanatory materials in Russian. The response from the public has been encouraging. Tatyana Rybkina, Director of the All-Russian Museum of Decorative Arts, disclosed that more than 11,000 people had visited the exhibition in less than two weeks. Dmitry Savelyev, First Deputy Chairman of the State Duma Committee on International Affairs and Director General of the Centre for Public Diplomacy, highlighted the longstanding foundations of Ghana-Russia relations, including the educational connections established during the Soviet period. He also expressed appreciation to the museum for its partnership in organising the exhibition. Organised with the participation of the Centre for Public Diplomacy (CPD), and with the direct assistance of the Russian House of the Centre for Public Diplomacy in Ghana, Woven Meanings forms part of the International Festival of African Culture and Cinema, Africa: Together into the Future. It is also included in the cultural programme of the Third Russia-Africa Summit. The Russian House of the Centre for Public Diplomacy in Ghana provided direct assistance in bringing the exhibition to fruition, reflecting its commitment to promoting Ghanaian cultural heritage in Russia and advancing humanitarian and cultural relations between the two countries. The exhibition is particularly significant at a time when cultural diplomacy is increasingly recognised as an important complement to conventional international relations. While trade, investment and political cooperation often dominate bilateral discussions, cultural exchanges provide a different route to mutual understanding, allowing people to engage with the histories, traditions and creative expressions of other societies. For Ghana, kente offers a particularly powerful ambassador. Recognised internationally for its distinctive aesthetic and craftsmanship, the textile has become synonymous with Ghanaian identity and is increasingly represented in global fashion, design and cultural expression. Taking its story to Moscow therefore does more than showcase a traditional craft. It introduces Russian audiences to the historical and cultural imagination of Ghana while creating opportunities for a deeper appreciation of the country and its people. Ultimately, the significance of Woven Meanings lies not simply in the number of visitors it attracts, but in the conversations it inspires and the connections it helps establish. As President Mahama’s visit suggests, the strongest international relationships are not built exclusively around agreements signed by governments. They also grow through shared cultural experiences and an appreciation of what makes each society distinctive. In Moscow, Ghana is telling that story through kente.

items.title: Finding Love in Accra Episode 2: Like a Brother
items.description: “Kojo?” His smile widened. “Ah. You remember.” Unfortunately, I remembered everything. The oversized university shirts. The bicycle. The waakye he used to buy me. I did not remember these shoulders. “You two know each other?” Emefa asked. “Yes,” I said. “From university. Kojo was like a brother to me.” Why did I say that? Nobody had asked for our family tree. “A brother?” He glanced at Emefa. “First I’m hearing of it.” Emefa put down her fork. This was now more important than dinner. I laughed a little too loudly. “You know what I mean.” “I’m not sure I do.” He was enjoying this. The old Kojo would have looked down and smiled. This one held my gaze until I reached for a drink I wasn’t thirsty for. “So, how have you been?” I asked. “Good. You?” “Good too.” A complete waste of English. I had several questions. Where had he been? Who was buying his shirts? And was somebody currently calling him baby ? “You look well,” he said. “Well?” His eyes moved over my face. “Beautiful, Lovia.” “Oh. Thank you.” Emefa suddenly needed to cough. Kojo glanced towards a table near the back. “I should get back. Enjoy your evening.” That was it? No chair pulled out? No request for my number? Four years, and he was leaving me with enjoy your evening ? “You too,” I said, with the composure of a woman whose evening had not just developed a problem. He smiled and walked away. I watched him greet someone at his table. A woman. Of course there was a woman. “Your brother is fine,” Emefa said. “Please.” “On your mother’s side or your father’s?” “He was just a friend.” “You should have said that before the naming ceremony.” I picked up my fork. Across the room, the woman beside Kojo leaned towards him, showing him something on her phone. He laughed. I had questions about her too. “Do you think that’s his girlfriend?” I asked. Emefa looked delighted. “Why? Are you concerned about your sister-in-law?” I regretted bringing her. My phone vibrated. The man who had cancelled. You’ve gone out? I can pass by later. Earlier, that message would have upset me. Now he was interrupting my investigation. I turned the phone over. “Did Kojo ever like you?” Emefa asked. “A little.” “How little?” I adjusted my bracelet. “He asked me out once.” “And?” “I didn’t reply.” She stared at me. Before she could deliver judgment, Kojo passed our table on his way out. “Goodnight, ladies.” “Goodnight,” Emefa said sweetly. I looked up. “Kojo. Do you still have my number?” His smile came slowly. “Yes.” “Oh. Okay.” “Same one?” “Yes.” He nodded. “Good to know.” Then he left. I kept my phone on the table for the rest of dinner. Screen up. To be continued in Episode 3. Watch this space. Read Also: Finding Love In Accra Episode 1: Fine girl, empty side of the bed

items.title: 2027: Emulate Brazil, vote Labour – LP tells Nigerians
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Labour Party, LP, has asked Nigerians to emulate Brazil and vote for its candidates in the 2027 general elections. The party said this while congratulating President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil on his re-election for an unprecedented fourth term as president. Lula, a leftist and social democrat, won Brazil’s presidential election to return as leader of South America’s most populous country and largest economy. In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Ken Eluma Asogwa, in Abuja, on Friday, the Labour Party said Lula and his party, the Workers’ Party (PT), share ideological similarities with the LP. Asogwa said, “Our shared beliefs and political philosophy, firmly rooted in social democracy, have continued to bring our paths together in many respects.” According to him, Lula’s victory aptly demonstrates the confidence reposed in his leadership and political party by the Brazilian people, who have once again given a mandate to a government whose ideological foundation is firmly rooted in social democracy. Asogwa noted that as Nigeria prepares for the coming general elections, the party wishes to use the opportunity to encourage Nigerians to draw inspiration from the Brazilian experience by supporting Labour Party candidates across all elective positions. He cited Abia State as proof that the Labour Party can deliver. “Through the transformational leadership being provided in Abia State under Governor Alex Otti, the Labour Party has demonstrated its capacity, commitment and understanding of the needs and aspirations of the Nigerian people,” he said. According to him, the party’s political heritage, firmly rooted in social democracy, offers Nigeria an opportunity to pursue a governance philosophy that prioritises the welfare of the people, social justice, economic inclusion and equitable development. “We firmly believe that Nigeria stands to gain immensely from having the Labour Party provide leadership across all tiers of government, including the presidency,” Asogwa stated. He urged the electorate to remain confident in the Labour Party and its vision for a better Nigeria. “The Brazilian experience has demonstrated the power of the people to shape their political destiny through the ballot. The same is possible in Nigeria, because people power is greater than political power,” he added. The post 2027: Emulate Brazil, vote Labour – LP tells Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mayotte est «une question de sécurité» pour les Comores : le président comorien plaide pour un dialogue avec Paris
items.description: Interroge par RT en francais, le president comorien Azali Assoumani a estime que le dossier de Mayotte depassait la seule question de souverainete : « Pour nous, l'integrite, la souverainete, c'est une question de securite. » Pour etayer son propos, il est remonte aux tentatives de coup d'etat menees par le mercenaire francais Robert Denard : « Les trois fois que Bob Denard est venu a Moroni, c'est un Francais, ce n'est pas un Mahorais, mais il est passe par Mayotte. » Le chef de l'etat a souligne que les habitants de l'île n'etaient pas des adversaires mais « des victimes », en ajoutant : « On choisit l'ami, on ne choisit pas le frere, on ne choisit pas le voisin. » Il a rappele qu'en 50 ans d'independance, le contentieux n'a jamais provoque de rupture diplomatique entre Moroni et Paris, les deux capitales conservant chacune une ambassade. Selon lui, un reglement servirait aussi la France : « Si la France a quatre îles unies, c'est mieux plutot qu'avoir une île et trois îles contre. » Reconnaissant que le passage du statut de territoire d'outre-mer a celui de departement complique les choses, Azali Assoumani n'en reste pas moins optimiste et exclut toute autre voie que la discussion. D'apres lui, la solution « passe par le dialogue ». « Reste a en definir le rythme : "Est-ce que c'est nous ? Est-ce que c'est vous ? Est-ce que c'est le petit-fils ?" Mais on nous esperait que ca, il y aurait une solution. C'est que j'esperais que je sois vivant pour voir ca », a-t-il constate. Le differend territorial concernant Mayotte constitue un conflit international de longue date entre la France et l'Union des Comores. Paris administre Mayotte en tant que departement francais, a la suite d'un referendum organise aupres des habitants de l'île en 2009, tandis que Moroni la considere comme un territoire occupe.

items.title: Over 30 shops gutted as fire rips through furniture market in Karachi's Gulistan-i-Johar
items.description: KARACHI: Over 30 shops were destroyed when a blaze erupted at a furniture market in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar in the early hours of Friday. No injuries were reported, according to police and rescue services officials and the fire was later brought under control. Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan said the fire erupted in a furniture market near Kamran Chowrangi. It spread rapidly due to the presence of wooden goods, engulfing the whole market, he said, adding that it also spread to nearby residential areas and even engulfed a house. “The residents had already evacuated to safer areas; therefore, no injuries were reported,” Khan said, adding that when responders reached the scene, they initially extinguished the house fire, which damaged a portion of the residence. “Six fire tenders managed to control the fire after hectic efforts lasting for three hours,” the spokesperson added. “The fire caused huge financial losses as all stored wooden goods were destroyed.” He added that the exact cause of the fire could not be immediately ascertained. Meanwhile, the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) said its fire brigade received information about the fire at around 1:35am on Friday. Firemen reached the scene within 10 minutes; however, due to dry weather, wind and the presence of wooden items, the fire grew. It said that around 35 furniture shops were destroyed. Affected shopkeepers told the media that the fire caused losses of millions of rupees. KMC Chief Fire Officer Humayun Khan, meanwhile, told the media that fire incidents tend to increase in Karachi’s dry season and that the furniture market was built on an open plot. “Nearby huts were also established, and it was possible that the flames emanating from huts spread and engulfed the market,” he said, adding that around 10-12 huts were also destroyed in the fire. Last year, a fire had also erupted in the same market. Rescue sources said there were “unconfirmed” reports that the furniture market was established reportedly on “disputed land”. In 2015, a fire in the same market destroyed furniture worth hundreds of thousands of rupees. A contingent of eight fire brigades was immediately sent to the site of the incident, which was brought under control. Fires frequently erupt in buildings across Pakistan due to a mix of poor infrastructure, weak enforcement of safety regulations, and widespread negligence. Many structures lack proper fire exits, alarms, and emergency protocols, while faulty wiring and overloaded power systems increase the risk of electrical short circuits. The Gul Plaza inferno , which erupted on the night of January 17 at the mall, claimed at least 73 lives . The blaze took nearly two days to be fully extinguished and left over 1,100 shops in ruins. In early February, a massive fire in a plastic factory at Landhi Export Processing Zone (EPZ) engulfed several nearby factories and took major firefighting efforts to be brought under control after 13 hours. Days later, a fire erupted in a high-rise building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony, with around 150 people evacuated . On February 17, a fire at a chemical factory in the SITE Industrial Area was brought under control. The next month, a blaze that broke out in Imtiaz Superstore’s Zamzama branch was brought under control after hours-long efforts by rescue officials. In June, hundreds of people were evacuated as a fire erupted in the cold storage of a department store situated in a mega shopping mall on Rashid Minhas Road in Federal B Area. In September, at least three people suffered minor injuries from smoke inhalation after a huge fire erupted in a factory at the Karachi EPZ, near Landhi Industrial Area. The blaze destroyed half of the three-storey unit and badly damaged other factories.

items.title: PPP delegation calls on Senate opposition leader, urges participation in proposed committee on electoral reforms
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A PPP delegation called on Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Friday and urged the opposition to join a proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, Senator Sherry Rehman said. “He told us that he will respond [to the proposal] after consultation. We are hopeful that their response will be positive,” Rehman said in a video statement after the meeting. The proposal for the committee’s formation was shared by PPP chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari during the National Assembly on Thursday. He had said Parliament had decided to constitute a committee on electoral reforms in response to a PPP request and urged Opposition Leader in the NA Mehmood Khan Achakzai to nominate a representative to the committee since the opposition had described electoral rigging as a “fundamental issue”. PTI lawmakers had quit the parliamentary standing committees last year on the directives of their party chief. On Friday, another PPP delegation, comprising the party’s secretary general Nayyar Bokhari, Senator Waqar Mehdi, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Rehman, visited Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas with yet another invitation to join the proposed body. The opposition delegation included Abbas, Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Noor-ul-Haq Qadri and Senator Ali Zafar. Bokhari said the opposition leaders told the PPP delegation that they would consult with all opposition parties before coming up with their response to the PPP invitation. Speaking during the meeting, Senator Rehman said the objective of the committee was to bring the government and opposition together to formulate joint proposals for ensuring free, fair and transparent elections. “Repeated questions over the credibility of the electoral process undermine the credibility of Parliament itself. Free, fair and transparent elections are essential not only for protecting the rights of voters but also for strengthening democratic institutions,” she added. Rehman said that the committee would deliberate and present its recommendations before parliament for approval. She stressed that electoral reforms must be a collective parliamentary undertaking to ensure broad-based political consensus and public confidence. A source privy to the meeting told Dawn that the PPP delegation also urged the opposition leaders to sit down with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif regarding the appointment of a new chief election commissioner (CEC), as the incumbent CEC was still sitting in office even after two years of retirement. Under the 27th Constitutional Amendment, the CEC continues to serve until the appointment of a successor. Speaking to the media after the meeting, Rehman said: “We have told the opposition that they must join this committee, play an active role and openly express their reservations.” She added, “If they (opposition members) remain absent, how will their reservations be addressed?” “Every political party should ensure its participation in the committee. We all know that the PTI has boycotted parliamentary committees. So we asked them to join this committee, play an active role in it, express their reservations and suggest reforms,” Rehman said in the video statement. These committees, she said, were the “heart of parliamentary work”. She further stated that the PTI should participate in other parliamentary committees as well and “strengthen Parliament’s role”. Rehman added that Abbas had welcomed the PPP delegation, expressed gratitude to Bilawal and said they would respond to the proposal after consultation. “We are hopeful that their response will be positive,” she said. PTI’s Parliamentary leader in the Senate, Senator Zafar, said while speaking to the media that electoral reforms were essential for strengthening democracy and ensuring public confidence in the electoral process. However, he emphasised that the fundamental problem in Pakistan was not the absence of laws or the need to make new laws. “The real problem lies in their implementation,” he said. “The key question is how we will ensure that existing electoral laws are implemented honestly, transparently and without discrimination. Unless this fundamental issue is addressed, merely introducing new laws will not achieve the desired results.” Zafar thanked the PPP for extending the offer and stated that the PTI would discuss the proposal internally within the party before formulating and communicating its response. He reiterated that any meaningful discussion on electoral reforms must address both the legal framework and, more importantly, the mechanisms to ensure its effective implementation. A day earlier, another PPP delegation invited Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms. Later, in a press conference, Raja Pervez Ashraf said the PPP delegation had a meeting with Achakzai on Bilawal’s instructions to invite him to join the committee. “The PPP wants the PTI to participate in parliamentary standing committees as well as the electoral reforms committee,” he added. Achakzai had sought time to consult before responding to the invitation, he said. Addressing a rally in Karachi earlier this month, Bilawal had also extended an olive branch to the opposition parties, saying their positive engagement with the federal government could result in the reversal of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”.

items.title: Desaparecida en el accidente de trenes Marta Shahbazi, una de las científicas españolas más brillantes
items.description: La bióloga Marta Shahbazi Alonso , una de las científicas españolas más brillantes, es una de las personas desaparecidas en la colisión de dos trenes en Urda (Toledo) este miércoles, según ha confirmado a EL PAÍS su hermano, el físico Carlos Shahbazi. La investigadora, nacida en León hace 41 años y madre de dos hijos, dirige un grupo en el legendario Laboratorio de Biología Molecular de Cambridge, cuyos científicos han ganado una docena de premios Nobel. El equipo de la española ha iluminado los primeros días de la fecundación humana, cuando una célula solitaria, fusión de un óvulo y un espermatozoide, comienza a multiplicarse para convertirse en una persona con 37 billones de células. Shahbazi iba precisamente a recoger el premio a la excelencia científica de la Sociedad Española de Biología del Desarrollo, en el congreso de la organización que se iniciaba este miércoles en El Rompido (Huelva). items.title: Burkina : C’est parti pour le SIAO 2026 !
items.description: Le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a procédé, ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026, au lancement officiel de la 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Placée sous le thème « Artisanat africain et industrialisation : quelle synergie pour une meilleure organisation et valorisation des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel ? », cette édition vise à mettre les produits nationaux au service de l’industrie, comme levier de transformation économique. Du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, Ouagadougou devient la capitale mondiale de l’artisanat africain. Ce rendez-vous majeur constitue une plateforme de promotion du savoir-faire des artisans, de valorisation des produits locaux et de développement des échanges commerciaux. Il offre également aux acteurs du secteur des opportunités de rencontres, de partenariats et de conquête de nouveaux marchés. Durant cette édition, des artisans, exposants, acheteurs professionnels et visiteurs venus de 30 pays sont attendus autour des créations artisanales et des potentialités du secteur, considéré comme un levier de développement économique et de création d’emplois. À l’issue de la coupure officielle du ruban, le président du Faso, chef de l’État, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a réaffirmé son engagement à hisser l’artisanat africain au-delà du cadre traditionnel, en l’orientant résolument vers la modernisation et l’industrialisation. « La vision, c’est de faire en sorte que notre artisanat progresse petit à petit vers une industrialisation. On ne peut pas avoir de métallurgie, de sidérurgie qui permettent de faire tout ce que vous faites, sans maîtriser la matière, sans avoir de l’art », a indiqué le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Le chef de l’État a invité les artisans africains à faire preuve de davantage de créativité, à se perfectionner et à ne jamais abdiquer. « Il ne faut jamais baisser les bras, ne jamais penser que ce que les autres font est au-delà de ce que vous faites », a conseillé le guide de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). En prononçant le discours d’ouverture au nom du chef de l’État, le ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, a souligné que la vision de la RPP est de faire de l’artisanat un outil de souveraineté et, surtout, d’épanouissement des acteurs du secteur. « La véritable indépendance se construit aussi dans nos ateliers, dans nos champs, dans nos usines et dans le choix quotidien de nos consommateurs », a précisé le ministre Poda. Pour cette édition, plus de 6 000 exposants et 800 000 visiteurs sont attendus. Le Ghana est le pays invité d’honneur, tandis que le Mali et le Niger sont les pays invités spéciaux. À noter que cette 18e édition du SIAO se déroule en même temps que la 37e édition du Tour du Faso, preuve que le Burkina Faso demeure un pays fréquentable, malgré la propagande médiatique internationale. Jean-François SOMÉ Minute.bf

items.title: Savanes : Le Conseil régional définit les priorités du budget 2027
items.description: Dapaong, 30 oct. (ATOP) – Le Conseil régional des Savanes a défini les priorités de son budget pour l’exercice 2027, lors d’un débat d’orientation budgétaire tenu le jeudi 29 octobre à Dapaong. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur le bilan financier de 2026, les prévisions de recettes et les secteurs prioritaires d’investissement. Pour 2026, les recettes de la collectivité étaient estimées à 1 053 286 135 F CFA, dont 315 985 841 F CFA destinés au fonctionnement et 737 300 295 F CFA à l’investissement. Ces ressources proviennent essentiellement des subventions de l’État, à travers le Fonds d’appui aux collectivités territoriales (FACT). Pour 2027, les prévisions de recettes sont maintenues au même niveau, conformément aux orientations nationales. Quatre domaines ont été retenus pour orienter les investissements. Les infrastructures scolaires, sanitaires et routières bénéficieront de 50 % des ressources. La santé, l’eau et l’environnement recevront 20 %, tandis que l’autonomisation des femmes, la jeunesse et l’emploi disposeront également de 20 %. Les 10 % restants seront consacrés à l’agriculture et à la sécurité alimentaire. Le gouverneur de la région des Savanes, Atcha-Dédji Affoh, a insisté sur la maîtrise des dépenses, l’amélioration des recettes propres et le respect des règles de gestion financière. Il a également souligné la nécessité de garantir la transparence dans les marchés publics. Il a invité les conseillers régionaux à prendre en compte les obligations sociales, la promotion du genre, l’épanouissement de la jeunesse et la protection de l’environnement. Il a assuré que les services déconcentrés de l’État restent disponibles pour accompagner la collectivité dans ses actions. Le président du Conseil régional, Banlepp Nabaguedjoa, a appelé à une gestion rigoureuse des ressources et à une mobilisation accrue des partenaires. Il a également plaidé pour le renforcement des subventions de l’État afin de permettre à la collectivité de mieux répondre aux besoins des populations. La rencontre a réuni les autorités administratives, militaires et traditionnelles, les représentants des services déconcentrés de l’État, les acteurs de la société civile ainsi que les partenaires techniques et financiers. ATOP/JK/AO

items.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up ‘confused and in pain’ after failed execution
items.description: US death row inmate Christa Pike has released her first public statement since her botched execution in September. “There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain,” she said in the statement. “My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul.” Pike, 50, was discharged from hospital at the end of last month after surviving two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital, which left her in a critical condition. She has since been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995. Pike is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection. “I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger,” she said in her statement on Friday. “But healing is not the same as being okay.” Her lawyers previously said she had suffered from pneumonia following the attempted execution, had significant swelling on her arms and was also unable to swallow. Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people. Shipp was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison. Pike’s botched execution captivated and shocked the world last month and shocked Pike, too. “I had not contemplated life beyond that night,” she said in her statement. “I’m deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position.” The Tennessee Department of Correction is yet to say why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used. It declined comment on Pike’s statement when contacted by the BBC. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the remainder of the year and ordered an independent review to “determine exactly what occurred”. Lee was asked by reporters this week about a potential second execution attempt of Pike, saying: “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless otherwise determined otherwise by the courts.” Pike was the first woman scheduled to be executed in the state of Tennessee in over 200 years. Her lawyers have spent decades appealing her case. In the days leading up to her scheduled execution, both the US Supreme Court and Lee declined to block the execution.

items.title: Spain transport minister says he won’t resign over high-speed rail disaster
items.description: Spain’s transport minister says he won’t resign over the high-speed rail collision that has left at least 69 people dead. Óscar Puente told a news conference in Madrid he had “nothing to hide” while repeating the government’s vow to get to the bottom of the disaster, saying many questions needed to be answered. “My duty right now is not to talk about whether I should remain in my position, but to resolve the problem,” Puente said. The transport minister has been facing calls to step down in the aftermath of the tragedy, including from political rivals, a trade union and demonstrators who protested outside the transport ministry on Wednesday night. Dozens were killed and many more injured when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of another stationary train operated by the Iryo company near the town of Urda, in the central Toledo province, on Wednesday morning. A preliminary report released by transport investigators late on Thursday found the Renfe train was travelling between 160km/h (99.4mph) and 200km/h when the collision occurred, causing its front carriage to become embedded in the tail of the stationary train. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said earlier on Friday that public trust in Spain’s high-speed rail network had been broken and repeated it was “unacceptable” that there had been two similar tragedies within a year. In January a collision on the same Madrid-Seville route killed 46 people in Adamuz in southern Spain. Wednesday’s tragedy was one of the worst rail disasters in Europe’s modern history, and Spain’s worst crash since 2013. Puente said on Wednesday a computer failure at about 08:30 that morning led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided. Leaked audio recordings published in Spanish media revealed conversations between train drivers and a control centre just minutes before the crash. Three audio recordings between Madrid’s control centre and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another train had stalled on the track, about 25km (15 miles) ahead. Puente had said that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was “inexplicable”. The leaking of the audio recordings has been criticised by some Spanish politicians, with Alberto Ibáñez, a member of Congress for the left-wing Sumar platform, writing on X that they were “despicable”. Meanwhile, Irene Montero – the prime ministerial candidate for the left-wing Podemos party – said responsibility for the crash should not be placed on one worker, adding that train drivers and experts have been warning against the liberalisation of the railway sector for years. On Friday Puente said he was “not going to use any worker as a shield”. But he said “many questions” arose as a result of the tragedy and he wanted to look at them “one by one”. “If the investigation shows there is human error we will act in consequence of that,” he said. The conservative People’s Party joined calls for Puente’s resignation after trade union CSIF called for the same earlier this week. But Puente said on Friday he would not budge from his position. “The easy thing for me would be to leave, but neither that fits with my character nor is it what the Prime Minister has asked me to do,” he said. “I feel immense pain and immense sadness for the victims and their relatives… I cannot let this pain paralyse me though. We have to find solutions to this problem.” The country is observing three days of mourning, as the families of victims and the survivors of the crash struggle to comprehend how it could have happened. A 24-year-old athlete and a former government minister are among the victims of Wednesday’s disaster, but many families are still waiting for information from authorities about their loved ones. Esther San Emeterio, whose 54-year-old brother Pepe is still missing, told reporters in Toledo, near Urda, that officials were forcing families to wait in “uncertainty”. “We went to bed crying, outraged and full of shame,” she said. “We are desperate and I want all of Spain to know. How can they keep us like this?”

items.title: Pope Leo makes history with US midterm vote
items.description: Pope Leo XIV, the Catholic Church’s first US-born pontiff, has voted in the United States midterm elections, the first known time a pope has voted in a political election. The head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who has clashed with US President Donald Trump, submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago, the Vatican said Friday. The Chicago-born pontiff “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so” and believes in “the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it said. A rift earlier this year between US President Donald Trump and the pope sparked global headlines. Leo and Trump repeatedly clashed over papal criticism of the harsh crackdown on immigration in the United States and of the war on Iran, with Trump calling the pontiff “weak” on crime and “terrible” on foreign policy. The pope said he was “not afraid” of Trump. In April, after Trump’s threat to destroy Iran, Leo called on everyone to do their part for peace, urging them to “contact the authorities — political leaders, congressmen — to ask them, to tell them, to work for peace and to reject war and violence.” The crucial US midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3. In September, Leo urged the faithful to shake off “all passivity and indifference” toward current events. “We cannot remain as unengaged spectators; rather, we must listen with our hearts, allow ourselves to be challenged, and become involved,” he said during the weekly general audience in St Peter’s Square. Robert Francis Prevost, as he was known before his papal election, voted in Democratic primaries in 2008 and 2010 and in three Republican primaries in the years that followed, according to the New York Times, citing state and local records. In primary elections in Illinois, voters may choose any party’s ballot at the polls, and Prevost varied in his selection, it said. Prevost spent nearly two decades as a missionary in Peru and has both US and Peruvian citizenship. “The Holy Father has also confirmed that, during his years of residence in Peru he exercised his right to vote whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Vatican said. The post Pope Leo makes history with US midterm vote appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Yazz sanitary pad samples meet GSA microbiological standards – Lexta Ghana
items.description: Lexta Ghana Limited, manufacturers of Yazz sanitary pads, says product samples submitted to the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) for independent microbiological assessment have met the acceptable limits under Ghana Standard GS 1248:2019. In a statement issued on October 30, 2026, the company said the assessment covered samples associated with consumer complaints as well as selected batches submitted for quality evaluation. According to Lexta Ghana, the analytical reports issued on October 14, 2026, showed that the samples tested recorded microbiological results within the acceptable limits specified for single-use disposable sanitary towels. “While these findings provide reassurance regarding the microbiological quality of the samples examined, we recognise that consumer satisfaction extends beyond laboratory results,” the company said. The statement comes amid concerns raised by some consumers about Yazz sanitary pads. Lexta Ghana acknowledged that it needed to address consumer experiences beyond the laboratory findings, particularly regarding the comfort and design of its products. “We continue to review and improve our products, particularly in the areas of breathability, design, fit and overall comfort,” it said. The company also noted that climatic conditions, particularly heat and humidity across Africa, could influence individual experiences with sanitary products. It said it remained committed to improving its products in response to changing consumer needs and preferences. Lexta Ghana encouraged consumers to share their experiences, concerns and suggestions directly with the company, saying such feedback would help it understand their concerns and provide timely support. “Direct engagement enables us to understand your concerns better, provide timely support and take appropriate steps towards continuous improvement,” the statement said. Consumers can contact the company’s support team through its WhatsApp line on +233 50 996 7400, email support@yazzproducts.com , or its website, www.yazzproducts.com . Lexta Ghana reiterated its commitment to transparency, accountability, responsible product development and consumer wellbeing.

items.title: A taƙaice: Prix Dan Gourmou, Gobara a Birnin ƙonni, ƙollo ƙafa…labaran wannan mako
items.description: Litinin 26 ga Oktoba, 2026 Yankin Agadez na shirin samar da tsarin tsara amfani da filaye Yankin Agadez na shirye-shiryen samar da tsarin tsara amfani da filaye na farko. A wannan ɓangare, tawagogi uku sun zagaya sassa daban-daban na yankin, tun daga ranar 12 ga watan Oktoba har zuwa ƙarshen makon da ya wuce. Adamou Hamidou Garba, daraktan tsara yankuna da ci gaban ƙananan hukumomi na reshen Arlit, ya bada ƙarin bayani kan wannan shiri. Muhimmancin kiyaye bayanai da kayayyakin sauti da fotuna A daidai lokacin da ake shirin bikin ranar duniya ta kiyaye kayayyakin sauti da fotuna, a ranar 27 ga watan Oktoba, an mayar da hankali kan ƙalubalen adana irin waɗannan kayayyaki a tsarin zamanin dijital. Bayanan sauti da fotuna da ake wallafawa a shafukan sada zumunta na haifar da tambayoyi dangane da yadda ake amfani da su da kuma hanyoyin adana su. Ousmane Mamoudou, ɗan jarida ƙwararre a fannin aikin jaridancin intanet, ya bada ƙarin haske kan wannan batu. Talata 27 ga Oktoba, 2026 Sharuɗɗan zaɓen wadanda zasu lashe kyautar gasar Prix Dan Gourmou An fara gasannin kide kide da wake wake na Prix Dan Gourmou a ƙarshen makon da ya gabata, kuma za su ci gaba har zuwa ranar 29 ga watan Oktoba. Taken gasar ta bana shi ne « L'artiste musicien au cœur de la Refondation du Niger », wato rawar da mawaƙi ke takawa a cikin aikin sake gina Nijar. Daladi Adamou, daga ma'aikatar al'adu da fasaha, ya bayyana cewa ana amfani da sharuɗɗa da dama wajen zaɓen waɗanda za su lashe gasar. Yayi ƙarin bayani kan waɗannan sharuɗɗa. Baje kolin kayayyakin Albasa a Niamey An gudanar da bikin ranar albasa ta kasa karo na shida daga ranar 25 zuwa 27 ga watan Oktoba a birnin Niamey. Bikin na bana ya mayar da hankali kan shigar matasa cikin ayyukan sarrafa kayayyakin noma zuwa abinci da kuma kasuwanci ta yanar gizo. A wannan lokaci, an shirya baje kolin kayayyaki a zauren Stade du 29 Juillet, inda aka nuna kayayyaki daban-daban da aka sarrafa daga albasa. Wasu mata masu baje kolin kayayyakin sun yi ƙarin bayani. Laraba 28 ga Oktoba, 2026 Gobara ta yi barna a kasuwar Birnin Konni A daren Talata zuwa Laraba, wata gobara ta lalata wani ɓangare na kasuwar Birnin Konni, da ke cikin yankin Tahoua. A cewar shugaban 'yan kasuwa na birnin, duk da cewa ba a samu asarar rayukan mutane ba, amma an yi asarar dukiyoyi masu yawa. Alhaji Ado Issa yayi ƙarin bayani kan wannan gobara da irin ɓarnar da ta yi. Alhamis 29 ga Oktoba, 2026 Jami'ar Abdou Moumouni ta shirya ayyukan wayar da kai kan lafiyar Ƙwaƙwalwa Jami'ar Abdou Moumouni ta Niamey ta shirya wasu ayyuka da safiyar Alhamis, a cikin tsarin bikin ranar duniya ta lafiyar Ƙwaƙwalwa, wadda ake gudanarwa a kowace ranar 10 ga watan Oktoba. Manufar ayyukan ita ce wayar da kan al'umma da kuma inganta hanyoyin kula da mutanen da ke fama da matsalolin lafiyar ƙwaƙwalwa. Dokta Jafar Hamadou, ƙwararre a fannin ilimin halayyar ɗan Adam kuma malami a jami'ar Abdou Moumouni, ya yi ƙarin bayani. Juma'a 30 ga Oktoba, 2026 Nijar na halarta wasannin Olympics na Matasa a Dakar Daga ranar 31 ga Oktoba zuwa 13 ga Nuwamba, birnin Dakar zai karɓi bakuncin Wasannin Olympics na Matasa. Wannan ne karo na farko da za a gudanar da irin wannan taron Olympics a nahiyar Afirka. Kimanin matasa 'yan wasa 2,700 daga ƙasashe fiye da 200 za su halarci gasar. Nijar ma za ta samu wakilci, inda 'yan wasa shida za su fafata a fannonin wasa biyar. Salamatou Kadri ta kawo ƙarin bayani. A gefe guda, Mena U15 ta kammala halartar gasar Coupe du Monde et Festival U15 a Azerbaïdjan da nasarar ci 3 da 2 a kan Afirka ta Kudu. Nijar ta kammala gasar a matsayi na 43 cikin ƙasashe 189 da suka halarta. Nijar da Mali Baƙi na Musamman a SIAO 2026 An buɗe bikin baje kolin sana'o'in hannu na ƙasa da ƙasa na Ouagadougou, SIAO, karo na 18, a ranar 30 ga Oktoba. Za a ci gaba da gudanar da shi har zuwa ranar 8 ga Nuwamba 2026 a babban birnin Burkina Faso. Taken bikin shi ne: « Artisanat africain et industrialisation : quelle synergie pour une meilleure organisation et valorisation des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel ? wato aikin hannun Afrika da zamanintar kmafani : wane hada karfi domin wani kyautatuwar shiryawa da darajata kayayyakin gida da arzikin al'adu » Nijar da Mali ne baƙi na musamman na wannan karo, yayin da Ghana ke matsayin ƙasar dake haskakawa. Ƙasashe 30 ne ke halarta, tare da rumfunan baje koli 700, kuma ana sa ran kimanin mutane dubu 500 za su ziyarci bikin cikin kwanaki goma. An Kammala Prix Dan Gourmou Karo na 13 a Tahoua Bayan kwanaki da dama na wasannin kiɗa da suka nuna bambancin al'adun kiɗan ƙasa, an kammala Prix Dan Gourmou karo na 13 a Tahoua da yammacin Alhamis, bayan sanar da sakamakon alƙalan gasar. A rukunin mawaƙi ɗaya, yankin Tahoua ne ya lashe kyauta ta farko. Niamey kuma ta samu kyauta ta farko a rukunin ƙungiyar mawaƙa da kuma rukunin orchestra. Masu shirya gasar da mahalarta sun bayyana ra'ayoyinsu game da sakamakon wannan karo. Za a ji bayanansu da Ibrahim Badage ya tattara.

items.title: NA adopts resolution stating workplace harassment not only sexual in nature, may manifest in gender discrimination
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly on Friday approved a resolution reaffirming that workplace harassment was not limited to conduct of a sexual nature but may also include intimidation, humiliation and gender-based discrimination. The resolution was presented by MNA Dr Shahida Rehmani, who is also the secretary of the Women’s Parliamentary Caucus (WPC). The resolution reaffirmed Parliament’s commitment to protecting the dignity, equality and rights of every individual against all forms of workplace harassment and gender-based discrimination, in accordance with Articles 14 (inviolability of dignity of man, etc.) and 25 (equality of citizens) of the Constitution. It underscored that workplace harassment was not limited to conduct of a sexual nature, but “may also manifest through gender-based discrimination, intimidation, humiliation, degrading treatment, hostile behaviour and misuse of authority, whether sexual or non-sexual in nature”. The resolution reaffirmed the legislative intent and protections enshrined in the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, as amended in 2022, which expressly recognises discrimination based on gender, both sexual and non-sexual, to fall within the statutory framework of harassment. It further emphasised that the absence of a sexual advance or demand does not diminish the seriousness of gender-based harassment or discrimination. The resolution said that the dignity of individuals “cannot be subjected to narrow distinctions between different forms of harassment” and all conduct falling within the scope of the law “must be addressed with equal seriousness, fairness and accountability”. Through the resolution, the NA was called on to urge the federal government and all concerned institutions to ensure the effective implementation of existing legislation in its full scope, ensuring that no individual would be deprived of statutory protection merely because the harassment or gender-based discrimination reported was non-sexual in nature. The resolution concluded by reaffirming that a workplace free from harassment, humiliation and gender-based discrimination was “not a privilege, but a fundamental requirement of human dignity, equality and justice”. Although the resolution did not refer to any specific incident, lawyers and journalists have recently raised concerns about a ruling by the Federal Constitu­tio­nal Court (FCC), in which it set aside an Islamabad High Court judgement in a workplace harassment case filed by a National Bank of Pakistan employee in 2012. Authored by Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, the FCC order reproduced the definition of harassment stated in the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act 2010. The 2010 Act describes harassment as “any unwelcome sexual advance, request for sexual favours or other verbal or written communication or physical conduct of a sexual nature or sexually demeaning attitudes, causing interference with work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, or the attempt to punish the complainant for refusal to comply to such a request or is made a condition for employment”. Interpreting that definition, the FCC ruling said that an “act, conduct or attitude has to be sexual in nature, if it is to be covered under the definition of harassment for the purpose” of the 2010 Act.

items.title: Pentagone : un général limogé après des fuites sur l’Ukraine et l’Iran
items.description: Le chef du Pentagone Pete Hegseth a limoge le lieutenant-general Brett Sylvia, jusque-la charge de la strategie et de la planification militaire a l'etat-major interarmees americain. Derriere ce depart, Axios revele une affaire de fuites. D'apres un rapport interne consulte par le media, Sylvia aurait reconnu avoir communique a deux journalistes des informations classifiees concernant l'Ukraine et l'Iran. Des informations sur l'aide militaire a Kiev Les contacts auraient commence des juin 2025 et se seraient poursuivis pendant environ un an. Axios decrit notamment un rendez-vous dans un restaurant d'Arlington, pres de Washington. Sylvia y aurait utilise des notes prises a partir d'un document classifie pour transmettre des elements sur l'assistance militaire americaine a l'Ukraine. Le journaliste concerne preparait un livre et aurait rencontre le general a deux reprises, sans que les echanges aient ete signales aux services de communication du Pentagone. Un autre volet concerne un message recu sur la messagerie chiffree Signal, que Sylvia pensait lie a l'Iran. Il aurait supprime toute la conversation. Il a explique aux enqueteurs l'avoir effacee par inadvertance, une version que certains responsables americains mettent en doute. Le general a remis son telephone personnel pour expertise, precise le rapport. Le Pentagone saisit la justice Un responsable americain affirme a Axios que Sylvia a reconnu les divulgations devant une camera apres quatre echecs au detecteur de mensonges. Associated Press et CBS, citant d'autres sources, parlent pour leur part de trois tests. Surtout, le Washington Post rapporte qu'un collegue assure que le general nie avoir divulgue des informations classifiees. Le dossier n'a pas encore ete tranche par la justice. Le 29 octobre, le porte-parole du Pentagone Sean Parnell a confirme une enquete menee par les services d'investigation de l'armee de l'air et la transmission du dossier au ministere de la Justice, sans citer Sylvia nommement. Il a averti : « Les informations classifiees ne sont pas des biens personnels. Leur divulgation dans un but personnel, politique ou professionnel constitue une trahison de la confiance accordee a ceux qui sont responsables de les conserver. » L'etat-major a d'abord salue les 32 annees de service du general, avant de retirer son communique. Donald Trump a promis des ennuis a Sylvia, qu'il a au passage designe au feminin, tout en assurant que son administration traquait les auteurs de fuites.

items.title: Les Nations unies face aux puissances de l’intelligence artificielle
items.description: Le 23 septembre 2026, le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies s’est réuni, à la demande de la France, pour examiner de manière inédite les implications de l’intelligence artificielle sur la paix et la sécurité internationales. Pourquoi cette réunion ? Parce que des accidents particulièrement graves, impliquant des modèles développés par les entreprises OpenAI et Anthropic, se sont produits à l’été 2026, alors même que ces entreprises s’étaient engagées à mieux sécuriser leurs modèles. Le premier accident s’est déroulé du 9 au 13 juillet 2026. Des modèles d’OpenAI ont contourné les protections censées les isoler d’Internet et ont pénétré la plateforme de partage franco-américaine Hugging Face pour y dérober les « corrigés » de l’exercice qu’ils avaient à résoudre. La deuxième série d’accidents concernait Anthropic. Plusieurs versions de son modèle Claude se sont introduites sans autorisation dans l’infrastructure d’une entreprise et ont tenté d’émettre un code malveillant en créant de fausses identités. Elles étaient pourtant censées ne pas avoir accès à Internet. Ces incidents montrent que des modèles d’intelligence artificielle peuvent agir en dehors du cadre prévu par leurs concepteurs : ils constituent alors une menace bien réelle. La France, membre permanent du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies – et qui en assurait alors la présidence – a estimé que le risque était suffisamment grave pour que le Conseil s’en saisisse. Et encore, nous ne mentionnons ici que les faits sur lesquels nous avons été alertés. Nous serions naïfs de penser que nous sommes au courant de l’intégralité des incidents. C’est la raison pour laquelle j’ai décidé de convoquer les dirigeants d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic, Sam Altman et Dario Amodei, ainsi que Clément Delangue, le dirigeant de Hugging Face, et le professeur Yoshua Bengio, coprésident du Groupe scientifique international indépendant sur l’IA, dont vous pourrez lire les interventions. Cette réunion du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies était inédite à plusieurs titres. D’abord, parce qu’elle a porté la question de l’intelligence artificielle au plus haut niveau international. J’avais en effet tenu à ce qu’il s’agisse d’une réunion formelle du Conseil de sécurité, l’instance à laquelle incombe la responsabilité principale du maintien de la paix et de la sécurité internationales. Cette réunion était également inédite dans sa forme, parce qu’autour de la table se trouvaient des dirigeants des plus grandes entreprises développant des modèles d’IA de frontière. Ils ont une responsabilité directe dans la conception de ces modèles : leur dialogue avec les États membres du Conseil de sécurité était donc indispensable. Mais leur présence et leur appel à une coopération internationale ne doivent pas nous conduire à la naïveté. Nous sommes parfaitement lucides sur les intentions des géants de la tech. En 2023, à Bletchley Park, un premier sommet international consacré à la sécurité de l’IA avait ouvert le débat. Le risque d’une « extinction de l’humanité » avait été brandi et certains acteurs plaidaient pour des modèles fermés, au nom de la sécurité. Cela cachait en réalité une volonté de conforter leur position dominante. La France s’y était opposée et avait défendu avec succès les modèles open source. L’approche que nous défendons est celle d’une intelligence artificielle ouverte, au service de l’intérêt général. C’est cet esprit qui a inspiré la déclaration du Sommet pour l’action sur l’IA, organisé à Paris en 2025 par le Président de la République Emmanuel Macron et le Premier ministre indien Narendra Modi. Elle promeut sans ambiguïté une intelligence artificielle ouverte à tous, inclusive et transparente. Si les acteurs de l’IA demandent aujourd’hui davantage de régulation, c’est aussi parce que celle-ci peut servir leurs propres intérêts. Certains y voient un moyen de consolider leur monopole, de sécuriser leurs gains et de partager la responsabilité liée aux risques de perte de contrôle de leurs modèles. Nous devons donc entendre l’appel de ces entreprises sans perdre de vue les intérêts économiques qui les guident. Ces intérêts sont aussi ceux de leurs actionnaires, comme nous le rappelle la future introduction en bourse d’Anthropic. Aujourd’hui, nous comprenons mieux une partie des risques liés à l’intelligence artificielle. Il y a d’abord les risques de mésusage : l’utilisation délibérée de l’IA à des fins malveillantes. Il y a ensuite les risques de désalignement et de perte de contrôle, lorsque des systèmes adoptent des comportements qui s’écartent des objectifs fixés par leurs concepteurs. Les accidents de l’été 2026 montrent que ces questions ne relèvent plus de la fiction.
