items.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to boost cooperation in oil, refineries and minerals
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed on Friday to strengthen strategic cooperation in oil storage, refinery upgrades, crude oil and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) procurement, and the minerals sector to promote bilateral economic ties, according to a statement issued by the Petroleum Division. Saudi Arabia also announced the immediate introduction of same-day visa processing for Pakistani citizens at its embassy in Islamabad. Pakistan has been planning to boost domestic storage for crude oil and refined products to increase its energy security. With no strategic petroleum reserves, the country has been left exposed to oil supply shocks resulting from the US-Iran war that has choked supplies through the Strait of Hormuz . The developments were announced after Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik met Saudi Arabia’s new ambassador to Pakistan, Dr Rajeh bin Tami Al-Baqami, to discuss opportunities for enhancing cooperation in the mining, petroleum and energy sectors, including strategic oil storage, refinery upgrades, LPG supplies and commercial engagement. The minister appreciated the longstanding strategic partnership between the two countries and said Pakistan had approved a tax-neutral bonded policy modelled on international energy hubs such as Fujairah and Singapore , according to the statement. “Under this framework, Saudi companies can establish commercial oil reserves in Pakistan without local tax liabilities, offering an opportunity to diversify maritime transit risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab while facilitating access to Asian markets,” the statement said. “The petroleum minister highlighted that strategic oil storage facilities in Pakistan would provide Saudi Arabia with greater flexibility in managing supply routes and accessing regional markets,” it added. The statement further quoted the minister as saying that Pakistan planned to develop a major petroleum storage and refining complex at Hub in Balochistan under the guidance of Technip Energies UK. “The proposed facility, supported by the prime minister and the chief of defence forces, will have the capacity to accommodate Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) and strengthen Pakistan’s potential as a regional energy corridor serving Central Asian and Chinese markets,” the statement quoted Malik as saying. Malik also briefed the ambassador on investment opportunities under Pakistan’s ongoing refinery upgradation programme, which aims to modernise domestic refining infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and facilitate a transition to Euro-5 fuel standards. He said the programme offered significant opportunities for Saudi investment and participation in Pakistan’s refining sector. Appreciating Saudi Arabia’s support during recent global market disruptions, the minister thanked the Saudi authorities at Yanbu port for prioritising crude oil shipments to Pakistan. He also discussed coordination with Saudi Aramco to increase crude oil procurement and arrange dedicated LPG shipments to meet Pakistan’s energy needs, particularly amid an anticipated rise in domestic gas demand during winter. Both sides underscored that the strong defence and strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia provides a foundation for broader regional peace, stability and economic cooperation. The Saudi envoy expressed Riyadh’s deep appreciation for Pakistan’s longstanding support, saying the two countries stood together in all circumstances. The ambassador emphasised that the two countries’ defence and energy cooperation frameworks aimed to promote peace, stability and economic growth across the region. The minister also announced that the Saudi embassy in Islamabad had introduced same-day processing of visa applications for Pakistani citizens to facilitate travel and strengthen business, cultural and people-to-people exchanges. Malik invited Saudi Arabia’s Vice Minister of Mining, Khalid al-Mudafier, to attend the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, scheduled to be held in Islamabad on November 12 and 13, highlighting further opportunities for cooperation and investment in Pakistan’s minerals sector. Both sides expressed their commitment to strengthening their longstanding relationship through enhanced cooperation, investment and mutually beneficial partnerships in the energy and petroleum sectors. The minister assured the ambassador that Pakistan deeply valued its historic relationship with Saudi Arabia and remained committed to expanding cooperation across strategic sectors. Earlier in July, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed authorities to increase the country’s strategic petroleum reserves as a cabinet committee approved amendments to the oil refining policy.

items.title: Football : La CAF fait machine arrière et maintient la CAN tous les deux ans
items.description: Le Comité exécutif de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a décidé à l'unanimité, le jeudi 29 octobre 2026, de rétablir la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations (CAN) tous les deux ans, abandonnant le projet d'une compétition quadriennale adopté en décembre 2025. Le président Patrice Motsepe justifie ce revirement par l'incapacité de la future Ligue des Nations africaine à générer à court terme les revenus nécessaires au football africain. La décision était attendue depuis la conférence stratégique de la CAF, tenue du 7 au 9 octobre 2026 au Cap-Vert. Patrice Motsepe y avait lui-même annoncé que le Comité exécutif réexaminerait le passage à un cycle de quatre ans, voté l'année précédente à Rabat. Jeudi, l'instance continentale a officialisé son revirement dans un communiqué publié sur son site internet, confirmant le retour à la périodicité qui a structuré l'histoire de la CAN pendant près de sept décennies. Au cœur de ce rétropédalage figure l'argument financier. La CAF avait initialement prévu de remplacer la CAN par une Ligue des Nations africaine, compétition panafricaine devant se disputer tous les deux ans. Or, l'instance reconnaît désormais que cette nouvelle épreuve nécessiterait « plusieurs années » avant de pouvoir apporter les ressources substantielles indispensables à la compétitivité et à l'autonomie financière du football africain. « Nous étions préoccupés par le nombre d'années nécessaires avant que la nouvelle compétition panafricaine proposée, la Ligue des Nations, conçue pour être identique à l'actuelle CAN et se disputer tous les deux ans, puisse apporter les contributions financières substantielles et les retombées nécessaires au développement du football africain », a déclaré Patrice Motsepe dans le communiqué officiel. Le président de la CAF a également inscrit cette décision dans une logique de défense des intérêts des 54 associations membres et des joueurs africains évoluant dans des clubs hors du continent. « La décision du Comité exécutif de la CAF de rétablir l'organisation de la CAN tous les deux ans vise à faire progresser, à protéger et à promouvoir les intérêts du football africain et des 54 associations membres de la CAF, ainsi que ceux des joueurs africains évoluant dans des clubs en dehors du continent », a-t-il précisé. Le calendrier des prochaines éditions a été arrêté. La CAN 2027 se tiendra au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda, une première co-organisation en Afrique de l'Est. Les éditions suivantes sont programmées en 2028, 2031 et 2033. L'absence d'édition en 2030 s'explique par la volonté de la CAF de respecter la tradition de la FIFA, qui veut qu'aucune compétition continentale majeure ne se déroule la même année que la Coupe du monde. La prochaine édition, prévue du 19 juin au 18 juillet 2027, constituera le premier test grandeur nature de cette nouvelle ère retrouvée. Lire aussi : Football : La CAN se tiendra désormais tous les 04 ans à partir de 2028 Minute.bf

items.title: Just Noting That Your Candy Corn Is Made of Bug Secretions
items.description: Here’s a tip if you ever want to ruin a Halloween party. Seek out the most squeamish-seeming adult or child you can find in the act of consuming candy corn. Then tell them they just filled their mouth with bug secretions. If this fact alarms you—or if you’re an inveterate hater of candy corn and thus think that you have been spared—I regret to inform you that by eating many classic Halloween candies, you are, to some extent, eating bugs. More precisely, you are eating a bug by-product that is in many cases listed on the package as “confectioner’s glaze.” This glaze is used on jelly beans, Milk Duds, Junior Mints, Whoppers, Lemonheads, and Sugar Babies, to name a few. This sounds innocent enough, until you understand that the glaze is shellac—a shiny, moisture-blocking resin that’s the product of lac bugs’ lifelong work. As the female lac bug pierces a tree with her needlelike mouthparts and sucks the sap out, she secretes a goo, also called lac, from a gland on her abdomen to form a cocoon of sorts. (Male lac bugs don’t do much besides mate and die after about four days.) Inside her lac coating—which hardens on contact with the air much like, well, a candy shell—she spends her life feeding and laying eggs, safe from predators. If all goes well, she completes her life cycle and dies in her resinous home. The amount of resin produced by each insect is virtually microscopic, but over time, enough of the bugs cluster on one branch to make an amount worth pouring over a batch of Raisinets. The process has been the same for thousands of years: Strip the resin from the bark, melt it down, remove any impurities (translation: bits of wood and bugs), let it harden, and break it into shards. One pound of finished shellac requires the secretions of 100,000 insects. For every shiny candy you eat, roughly a quarter of 1 percent is this bug by-product, Michelle Frame, a candy scientist, told me. Humans are still harvesting shellac because it’s not really like anything else—man-made, bug-made, or otherwise. Most adhesives that are strong enough to coat surfaces or give them such a high gloss aren’t food-safe. Shellac is. It also has an appealing reddish color, thanks to the naturally occurring laccaic acid in it, which can be used as a dye. Depending on the alcohol or solvent that shellac is mixed with, it can be used as a furniture polish, as nail polish, or to make hair spray shine. It’s sprayed on some fruits to extend their shelf life and used to coat many pills, both to slow the rate of absorption in the stomach and to mask the taste of bitter medicines. None of this is a compelling advertisement for shellac as a candy ingredient. “People sometimes panic, like, It’s in your furniture! ” Frame said. But all of those uses are evidence of shellac’s versatility, not a nefarious plot to get Americans to eat wood polish. Even if you restrict its applications to candy making, shellac, which is both natural and tasteless, is more useful than any alternative. For example, zein, a protein derived from corn, can be used as a vegan candy coating. But Frame, like many other food scientists, believes that zein is not as strong as shellac, nor is it as good at keeping moisture out. (It also smells like a wet dog while the candy is being made, she said—even though the smell does go away once it dries.) Really, the fact that so many candies contain a product made by insects shouldn’t be a surprise. “Even highly industrialized societies are heavily dependent on the products of other species,” Edward Melillo, the author of The Butterfly Effect: Insects and the Making of the Modern World , told me. (Melillo readily acknowledged his own dependence: “I love candy corn personally, so I eat a lot of shellac,” he said.) People eat meat and wear wool, silk, and leather. A beeswax candle might be burning in your house (or in your jack-o’-lantern) right now. Corn syrup, used in many candies, is extracted from a grass that humans selectively bred into a monster version of itself, then processed into sugar in industrial laboratories. People have used red dye that’s sometimes called carmine or cochineal extract, made from crunched-up cochineal bugs, for more than 2,000 years. The substance is responsible for the vibrant red in Nerds Gummy Clusters, some Airheads products, Good & Plenty, and other candies. Meanwhile, squishy treats such as marshmallows and gummy bears—and candy corn—still largely use gelatin made from animal collagen, found in bones, skin, and ligaments. Whether any of this counts as icky is, of course, a matter of taste. Plenty of people eat insects and ligaments on purpose and with aplomb. And whatever your personal threshold, we’re all eating bugs and other perhaps undesirable animal bits all the time. Insects, rodent hairs, and droppings are so unavoidable in many agricultural products that the FDA has a list of legally acceptable defects allowed in popular foods; chocolate is permitted to have 60 insect fragments and one rodent hair per 100 grams. (According to Frame, even this is not so alarming: “A bug leg is just a bit of protein that will go through you anyway,” she said.) As much as you may want to avoid thinking about it, virtually all Halloween treats are creations worthy of Frankenstein. Why not consume a little bug goo on the side?

items.title: Ouagadougou : Des experts outillent les marketeurs à l’Intelligence artificielle pour doper la performance
items.description: Une masterclass co-animée par le Dr Sambo Kalifa Sankara et Bili Edouard Tieno a réuni praticiens et dirigeants autour de cas concrets d’application de l’IA, le jeudi 30 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. L’enjeu : concilier gain de productivité, retour sur investissement et protection du patrimoine informationnel dans un contexte africain. Comment l’intelligence artificielle peut-elle servir concrètement la fonction marketing en Afrique, sans se substituer au jugement humain ni exposer les données stratégiques des entreprises ? C’est la question qui a structuré la masterclass intitulée « L’intelligence artificielle appliquée au marketing : Booster la performance marketing dans un contexte africain », co-animée par le Dr Sambo Kalifa Sankara, expert en intelligence artificielle, et Bili Edouard Tieno, expert en stratégie marketing. Dr Sankara présentant un panorama d’outils, généralistes ou spécifiquement dédiés au marketing Devant un auditoire composé de professionnels et de dirigeants, les deux intervenants ont déroulé une approche résolument opérationnelle. « Ce qui a été donné aux différents participants, c’est les bases de l’IA appliquées au marketing sur des cas concrets », a expliqué le Dr Sankara. Cinq cas précis ont été disséqués pour démontrer que l’IA permet de traiter plus rapidement des problématiques complexes et, surtout, de révéler « ce qui n’est pas visible à l’œil nu ». Un panorama d’outils, généralistes ou spécifiquement dédiés au marketing, a été présenté. Mais l’expert en IA a tenu à poser un préalable méthodologique. « On peut avoir tous les outils du marché, si vous n’avez pas bien défini votre besoin, vos outils ne vous servent absolument à rien », a-t-il prévenu. Le procès, a insisté Dr Sankara, consiste d’abord à penser le besoin, avant de choisir la technologie. Pour Bili Edouard Tieno, l’appropriation de l’IA par les métiers du marketing et du développement commercial n’est plus une option. « Aujourd’hui, c’est inéluctable. La fonction marketing au sein des organisations est le moteur de la pérennité, de la croissance et du développement des entités », a-t-il affirmé. L’IA doit être comprise comme « une prolongation de leur capacité, de leur potentiel », au service de l’efficience et de l’efficacité. Face à un environnement économique en mutation, M. Tieno a lancé un appel aux praticiens à se mettre à niveau pour assurer le succès des organisations et impacter positivement l’environnement immédiat. « On n’arrête pas le développement. Il faut composer avec le développement », a-t-il souligné. Pour Bili Edouard Tieno, l’appropriation de l’IA par les métiers du marketing et du développement commercial n’est plus une option Les témoignages recueillis à l’issue de la session confirment l’acuité des attentes. Joël Ki, directeur général de Wave Mobile Money au Burkina Faso, retient deux enseignements majeurs. « Côté AI, j’ai vraiment appris qu’il y a toute cette notion de sécurité, de confidentialité, de données, en tout cas de sécurisation de nos données, c’est super important », a-t-il confié. Sur le volet marketing, M. Ki a souligné la possibilité d’aller « très vite » et de « faire bien » en cumulant les fonctions marketing et l’intelligence artificielle. Mais son attention a été particulièrement captée par l’exigence de retour sur investissement. « Si on peut dépenser moins et générer beaucoup plus, c’est encore mieux avec l’AI », a-t-il fait savoir. Cette question de la maîtrise des données et du savoir-faire irrigue également les préoccupations de Mahamadi Rouamba, directeur général de TICAnalyse. Sans contester l’apport de l’IA, il invite à la prudence. « On n’a pas encore trouvé de meilleur outil de production que cela. Mais il faut faire très attention parce que c’est dans cette capacité également que l’on risque, en fait, de perdre beaucoup en termes de savoir-faire, en termes d’informations qui peuvent constituer un capital pour une entreprise », a-t-il conclu. Minute.bf

items.title: CAN: la CAF fait marche arrière et rétablit le rythme biennal
items.description: La Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) retrouvera son rythme habituel de deux ans. Réuni le jeudi 29 octobre 2026, le Comité exécutif de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a décidé à l’unanimité de revenir sur la réforme qui prévoyait une organisation tous les quatre ans. Une décision que son président, Patrice Motsepe, justifie par la défense des intérêts du football africain et les enjeux financiers liés à la future Ligue des Nations. C’est un changement de cap pour le football continental. La CAF a officiellement renoncé à son projet de faire disputer la CAN tous les quatre ans. À l’issue de sa réunion du jeudi 29 octobre 2026, son Comité exécutif a rétabli la périodicité biennale de la compétition, mettant ainsi fin à une réforme annoncée l’année précédente. Cette révision avait été évoquée par le président de l'instance, Patrice Motsepe, lors de la Conférence stratégique de la CAF, organisée au Cap-Vert du 7 au 9 octobre 2026. À cette occasion, le dirigeant sud-africain avait annoncé que le Comité exécutif réexaminerait la décision de passer à un cycle quadriennal. Dans un communiqué publié sur son site officiel, la CAF explique que ce réexamen s'appuie notamment sur les incertitudes entourant la mise en place de la nouvelle Ligue des Nations africaine. Cette compétition, envisagée comme un rendez-vous biennal devant remplacer l'actuelle CAN, nécessiterait plusieurs années avant de générer des ressources financières suffisamment importantes pour soutenir le développement du football africain. Patrice Motsepe a défendu le bien-fondé de cette nouvelle orientation. «La décision du Comité exécutif de la CAF de rétablir l’organisation de la CAN tous les deux ans vise à faire progresser, à protéger et à promouvoir les intérêts du football africain et des 54 Associations Membres de la CAF, ainsi que ceux des joueurs africains évoluant dans des clubs en dehors du continent», a-t-il déclaré. Le président de la CAF a également insisté sur les limites financières du projet de Ligue des Nations. «Nous étions également préoccupés par le nombre d’années nécessaires avant que la nouvelle compétition panafricaine proposée, la Ligue des Nations, conçue pour être identique à l’actuelle CAN et se disputer tous les deux ans, puisse apporter les contributions financières substantielles et les retombées nécessaires au développement du football africain, afin de rendre les compétitions de la CAF compétitives à l’échelle mondiale et financièrement autonomes», a-t-il expliqué. Concernant le calendrier, la prochaine édition de la CAN est prévue en 2027 au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda. Les éditions suivantes se tiendront en 2028, 2031 et 2033. «La prochaine édition de la TotalEnergies CAF Coupe d’Afrique des Nations aura lieu en 2027 au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda, et je suis convaincu qu’elle connaîtra un grand succès», a assuré Patrice Motsepe. Le calendrier continental devra toutefois tenir compte de celui des grandes compétitions internationales. La Coupe du monde de la FIFA étant programmée en 2030, les phases finales de la CAN et des autres compétitions de sélections nationales des confédérations pourraient ne pas se tenir durant cette année-là, conformément à la tradition de la FIFA. Pour le patron de l'instance dirigeante du football africain, cette décision constitue une orientation favorable à l'avenir du ballon rond sur le continent. «La décision du Comité exécutif de la CAF sert au mieux les intérêts du football africain et des 54 Associations Membres de la CAF. Elle contribuera également de manière significative au développement et à la croissance du football en Afrique», a-t-il conclu. En rétablissant la CAN tous les deux ans, la CAF privilégie ainsi la continuité de sa compétition phare et entend préserver les intérêts sportifs et économiques du football africain. Un retour à l'ancien rythme qui redessine déjà le calendrier des grandes échéances continentales pour les prochaines années. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article CAN: la CAF fait marche arrière et rétablit le rythme biennal est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Détournement présumé de 78 milliards de GNF : « C’est pour me nuire auprès du président de la République », se défend Mandian Sidibé
items.description: Poursuivi dans une affaire portant sur un montant présumé de 78 milliards de francs guinéens, l’ancien directeur général de l’Office guinéen de publicité (OGP), Mandian Sidibé, a plaidé non coupable, ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026, devant la chambre de jugement de la CRIEF. Pour sa défense, il affirme que les accusations portées contre lui viseraient à le discréditer auprès du président de la République : « C’est pour me nuire auprès du président de la République », a-t-il déclaré. L’ancien patron de l’OGP est poursuivi aux côtés de Pépé Haba et du comptable Aboubacar Sidiki Konaté pour des faits présumés de détournement de deniers publics, d’abus de fonction, de corruption, d’atteinte à la liberté d’accès et à l’égalité des candidats dans les marchés publics, d’usage illicite de biens par l’octroi d’avantages injustifiés, de concussion et de complicité. Le montant en cause est estimé à 78 milliards de francs guinéens. Pour rappel, le 15 juin dernier, la chambre de jugement de la CRIEF avait ordonné la remise en liberté de Mandian Sidibé pour des raisons de santé, après plus d’un an de détention, tout en le plaçant sous contrôle judiciaire. Elisa CAMARA L’article Détournement présumé de 78 milliards de GNF : « C’est pour me nuire auprès du président de la République », se défend Mandian Sidibé est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Disrupted LPG supply
items.description: THE petroleum minister’s explanation in the National Assembly that the recent closure of the Iran border has disrupted liquefied petroleum gas supplies and driven up prices identifies a major cause of the current crisis. The subsequent partial border reopening has failed to ease the shortage. While the closure may have triggered the present shortages and price hike, the problem recurs every winter. Pakistan produces only about a quarter of the LPG it needs. The rest is imported, mainly from Iran. The disruption of cross-border trade has therefore exposed the vulnerability of a market that depends heavily on external supplies. The Iran war has also complicated efforts to bring in more by sea. The minister says efforts are being made to increase seaborne supplies, but consumers have yet to see relief. The state must explain what additional volumes have been secured, and when they will arrive. Further, why were no contingency measures taken before the Iran border closure, especially when the authorities knew that the onset of winter would push up demand? The decision-makers owe an explanation to people suffering due to sudden shortages and price shock. That said, the current LPG supply disruption is only part of the wider story. LPG prices have historically surged as winter approaches, even without a major supply shock. This recurring pattern suggests that the crisis is not simply the result of border closure. Inadequate advance planning, weak market oversight and the failure to build reliable supply arrangements leave consumers exposed whenever demand rises or imports are interrupted. The consequences are particularly harsh for households without access to piped natural gas. Millions of families in northern Pakistan, remote and hilly areas, and parts of Punjab depend on LPG for cooking and, during colder months, heating. Low gas pressure and restricted supplies in connected areas also push more consumers towards cylinders, adding to demand. With the official price around Rs280 per kg and reported market rates reaching Rs500-800, an essential fuel has become unaffordable for many. Blaming the Iran border closure is but an attempt to cover up the ministry’s failure to do its basic duty: ensure adequate supplies ahead of the closure and enforce the official fuel price. Published in Dawn, October 30th, 2026

JOJ Dakar 2026 : Volker Türk salue « une étape historique »
items.description: À la veille de l'ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ), le Haut-Commissaire des Nations Unies aux droits de l'homme salue une étape historique pour le continent africain et rappelle que le sport est un levier au service de la dignité et de l'égalité. Dans une vidéo diffusée avant le lancement de des JOJ akar2026, le Haut-Commissaire des Nations Unies aux droits de l'homme, Volker Türk, a adressé un message appuyé aux athlètes, aux fédérations et au monde sportif. Il y rappelle que le sport peut rassembler au-delà des frontières, combattre la discrimination et permettre à chaque jeune, quelles que soient ses origines, de participer, de compétir et de se sentir inclus. Une première olympique en Afrique Volker Türk s'est d'abord adressé aux participants de cette quatrième édition estivale des Jeux de la jeunesse : « Je salue les milliers de jeunes athlètes qui se rassembleront à Dakar au Sénégal au cours des prochaines semaines. Ils entrent dans l'histoire en participant à la toute première manifestation olympique organisée en Afrique. » Pour lui, cet événement dépasse le cadre sportif : « Le sport porte en lui une promesse de dignité et d'égalité pour tous et toutes, tout comme les droits humains. » Il en tire un principe : « Les grands événements sportifs devraient être accessibles à tous et à toutes et se dérouler partout. » Le Haut-Commissaire a rendu hommage à celles et ceux qui œuvrent à tenir cette promesse « dans l'esprit de la Charte Olympique et de la Déclaration universelle des droits de l'homme ». Il a aussi souligné ce que le parcours d'un athlète a de commun avec le combat pour les droits : « La réussite sportive repose sur la ténacité, le courage et la détermination à se dépasser, quelle que soit son origine. » Une génération face aux grands défis Le message s'est ensuite tourné vers les enjeux qui attendent cette génération : « Les jeunes athlètes d'aujourd'hui font partie d'une génération qui fait face déjà à certains des défis majeurs de notre époque : l'urgence climatique, le racisme et la discrimination, les discours de haine, les inégalités, les conflits et les incertitudes liées à l'intelligence artificielle. » Volker Türk a plaidé pour que les jeunes soient associés aux décisions : « Les jeunes réclament une place à la table des décisions et la possibilité de contribuer aux choix qui façonneront leur avenir. Tout comme le sport, les droits humains ont besoin de personnes engagées. » Le Haut-Commissaire a rappelé l'initiative qu'il a lancée plus tôt dans l'année : « J'ai lancé l'Alliance mondiale pour les droits humains au début de cette année pour amplifier les efforts de toutes les personnes partout dans le monde qui défendent les droits humains. » Il a conclu par une invitation directe au monde sportif : « J'espère que les jeunes, les athlètes, les fédérations et autres du monde du sport rejoindront notre Alliance. Ne restez pas sur la touche, entrez sur le terrain, battez-vous pour les droits, et je vous souhaite beaucoup de succès pour les Jeux. »

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : un plan sanitaire articulé autour de 16 piliers
items.description: Le Sénégal a mis en place un dispositif sanitaire articulé autour de 16 piliers pour prévenir et gérer les risques liés aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Le plan, testé à travers deux exercices de simulation en octobre, mobilise plusieurs structures sanitaires et forces de sécurité, a indiqué jeudi le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Ibrahima Sy. Coordonné par le Centre des opérations d’urgence sanitaire (COUS), en collaboration avec le Comité d’organisation des JOJ (COJOJ), le SAMU national, les forces de sécurité et les partenaires techniques et financiers, le dispositif prévoit des centres médicaux avancés dans les trois zones de compétition : Dakar, Diamniadio et Saly. Il comprend également une polyclinique au village olympique, un hôpital pédiatrique de référence à Diamniadio ainsi que des circuits d’évacuation sanitaire organisés avec le SAMU national. Le ministre s’exprimait lors d’une rencontre avec le directeur régional de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) pour l’Afrique, le Dr Mohamed Yakub Janabi, en visite officielle au Sénégal pour accompagner les préparatifs sanitaires des JOJ Dakar 2026. Ibrahima Sy a précisé que le plan national avait été éprouvé lors d’un exercice de simulation sur table, le 15 octobre, puis d’un exercice grandeur nature, le 24 octobre, avec la participation de près de 180 personnes. « Les enseignements tirés ont permis d’apporter des mesures correctives au dispositif », a-t-il souligné. En parallèle, la surveillance épidémiologique est renforcée sur les sites de compétition, tandis que des contrôles sanitaires sont effectués à l’Aéroport international Blaise Diagne (AIBD), notamment dans un contexte marqué par les risques liés à Ebola et à la diphtérie. « Notre dispositif est en place, il a été testé et nous restons vigilants », a assuré le ministre, réaffirmant la volonté du Sénégal de garantir la sécurité sanitaire des premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse organisés sur le continent africain. Il a salué l’appui de l’OMS et des partenaires techniques et financiers, estimant que les acquis de cette mobilisation pourraient contribuer durablement au renforcement du système de santé national. Les JOJ Dakar 2026 sont prévus du 31 octobre au 13 novembre.

items.title: Rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 : la Fondation Wazni poursuit, pour la troisième année consécutive, l’accompagnement de dix jeunes filles
items.description: Conakry, 29 octobre 2026 – Dans le cadre du projet « Scolarisons 100 jeunes filles » , porté par la Fondation DiakaCamara, la Fondation Wazni accompagne depuis 2024 dix jeunes filles dans leur parcours scolaire et leur développement personnel. En s’associant à cette initiative, la Fondation Wazni a choisi de prendre en charge et de mentorer ces dix bénéficiaires, avec l’ambition de leur offrir les conditions nécessaires à leur réussite scolaire, à leur épanouissement et à la construction de leur avenir. À l’occasion de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, les dix bénéficiaires ont reçu, le 1er octobre à Conakry, leurs kits et équipements scolaires afin de débuter cette nouvelle année dans de bonnes conditions. Un accompagnement global La Fondation Wazni privilégie un accompagnement qui va au-delà de la prise en charge scolaire. Le dispositif comprend notamment la scolarité, les fournitures et les tenues scolaires, ainsi que des mesures destinées à faciliter le quotidien des bénéficiaires et à soutenir leur progression : goûter, transport, séances de révision et suivi régulier. Le programme intègre également des actions en faveur du développement personnel et de l’ouverture sur le monde professionnel, afin de permettre aux jeunes filles de découvrir de nouveaux environnements, de renforcer leurs compétences et de mieux se projeter dans leur avenir. Trois années de mentorat La poursuite de cet accompagnement en 2026-2027 marque une troisième année de mentorat auprès des dix jeunes filles. À travers un suivi régulier et personnalisé, la Fondation Wazni entend les accompagner dans leur progression, renforcer leur autonomie et les aider à construire leur projet d’avenir avec confiance. À travers sa participation au projet « Scolarisons 100 jeunes filles » , la Fondation Wazni réaffirme ainsi sa conviction que l’éducation constitue un levier essentiel d’émancipation, de développement personnel et d’accès aux opportunités. Céline Wazni, r eprésentante de la Fondation Wazni : « Investir dans l’éducation des jeunes filles, c’est investir dans leur potentiel et dans l’avenir de toute une génération. » À propos de la Fondation Wazni La Fondation Wazni œuvre en faveur de l’éducation et du développement social à travers des initiatives visant à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage et à favoriser l’accès des jeunes aux opportunités. Son action s’inscrit autour de sa signature : Former – Construire – Transformer. items.title: Début d’une opération de rapatriement volontaire de 400 migrants sénégalais du Maroc, ce vendredi
items.description: Au moins 400 Sénégalais séjournant dans les centres d’accueil des migrants d’Argoub et de Bir-Gandouz, dans le sud marocain, vont regagner le Sénégal dans le cadre d’une opération de rapatriement volontaire prévue pour démarrer ce vendredi. “Une opération de retour volontaire des compatriotes candidats à l’émigration irrégulière actuellement accueillis dans les centres d’Argoub et de Bir-Gandouz au sud du Maroc se déroulera cette fin de semaine et la semaine prochaine. 400 personnes se sont inscrites sur les listes”, a indiqué l'APS qui cite une source diplomatique. Dix bus pouvant chacun convoyer 40 passagers vont ainsi partir du Maroc sur la base d’un programme planifié de concerts avec les autorités marocaines. C’est ainsi qu’un premier convoi de trois bus doit quitter le royaume chérifien ce vendredi. D’autres départs sont prévus le mardi 3 novembre et le jeudi 5 novembre tandis qu’une autre opération de rapatriement est en préparation pour la deuxième semaine du même mois. Trois pirogues transportant au moins 500 passagers, dont 300 Sénégalais, ont été interceptées dans les eaux territoriales marocaines par la Marine royale entre le 19 et le 25 octobre, a rapporté la même source. Elle signale la présence de nombreux femmes et enfants, y compris des bébés, parmi les candidats à l’émigration partis des côtes gambiennes et sénégalaises Une source diplomatique confirme que l’arrivée en nombre de migrants pose des problèmes d’accueil dans les centres du sud du Maroc où 800 personnes originaires principalement du Sénégal, de la Gambie, du Mali et le République de Guinée ont été recensés ces derniers jours. items.title: Doctors Say a Rare Kind of Measles Is on the Rise
items.description: Each October, after the last of the tobacco has been harvested and the apple jam canned, Amish communities begin celebrating the months-long “wedding season.” Twice a week, hundreds of celebrants pack into a home to watch a young couple wed and share a meal. These gatherings, however joyful, add to the worries of Roberta Devers, a home-birth midwife in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. At her prenatal appointments, she’s been asking mothers-to-be: With all of the celebrations, how are you going to keep yourself safe from measles? In Pennsylvania, at least 1,398 people have been infected with measles this year, according to recent estimates from the state health department; the Amish community, which has significantly lower vaccination rates than other Pennsylvanians, has been especially hard hit. Experts caution that the actual number of infections is likely much higher. “Every house that I go into, either my pregnant mama has it, her husband has it and she’s going to get it, or a family member has it,” Devers told me last week as she drove from one patient appointment to another through Lancaster County’s rolling farmland. Measles can be especially dangerous during pregnancy, leading to low birth weight, early labor, and miscarriage; one of Devers’s patients recently miscarried at 17 weeks while she was fighting a measles infection. If more pregnant women get measles, the number of newborns who have measles will almost certainly rise too. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics , historical reports suggest that about a quarter of children born to mothers who are sick with measles in the days leading up to labor will likely acquire the disease. No data on the current rate of measles acquired in utero, which is known as congenital measles, are publicly available yet. But health-care providers working in Pennsylvania say it’s on the rise—perhaps at a scale not seen in decades, if ever. Before the measles vaccine was licensed in 1963, roughly 95 percent of Americans contracted the disease in childhood, making them immune by the time they entered their reproductive years. But people who are of childbearing age today have lived through historically low measles rates. That means that a number of unvaccinated adults, including pregnant ones, never caught measles in childhood and are therefore not immune—and are now contracting the virus during large outbreaks. About two-thirds of the cases reported in Pennsylvania this year have been in adults ages 18 to 49, some of whom appear to be passing on the disease during childbirth. In an October 19 advisory , the Pennsylvania Department of Health noted that congenital measles had been identified in the state for the first time in decades. “It’s gone from something we never see to something that we are now commonly seeing,” John Goldman, an infectious-disease physician at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center in Harrisburg, told me. The Atlantic ’s Tom Bartlett reported in August that an infant in Lancaster County, born to a mother who was severely ill with measles, was declared dead within 30 minutes after birth. [ Read: The measles-stricken mother who lost her newborn son ] Documenting an increase in congenital-measles cases is challenging. Case reports date back to at least the 1930s , but “no one has done any kind of systematic collection” of data, Adam J. Ratner, an infectious-disease pediatrician in New York, told me. The Pennsylvania Department of Health cannot release measles patients’ personal information, including their precise age, in order to protect their privacy, the deputy press secretary Stephanie Nojiri told me, and even if they could, no national definition for congenital measles exists to standardize tracking. Historically, doctors have diagnosed congenital measles when they observe a measles rash and other typical symptoms of the disease within the first 10 days of a newborn’s life. But that definition may unwittingly count some infants who contract measles in their first days of life outside the womb and miss counting infants with milder cases who do not present with a rash, Ratner said. Because congenital measles has historically been so rare, doctors know very little about its effects. Measles is known to wipe a person’s immune memory, making survivors highly susceptible to infections for years to follow; a 2019 study in children found that the virus demolished anywhere from 11 to 73 percent of antibodies and memory cells. And all people who contract measles are at risk of developing a rare but almost always fatal brain inflammation, subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, that can occur a decade or more after they contract the disease. But newborns can react to viruses differently than children even a few months older, which could mean that the effects of congenital measles deviate. That dangerous brain inflammation, for example, appears to occur more commonly and more quickly in congenital cases than in cases acquired after birth. For now, doctors are trying to pool what they do know. Ratner, who is a member of the American Academy of Pediatrics’ committee on infectious diseases, helped assemble new AAP guidance on how to treat congenital measles; he and his colleagues consulted doctors in Canada, which saw congenital-measles cases during an outbreak last year, but also had to extrapolate from how pediatricians treat measles in older children. John Goldman told me that he and other physicians had been following that guidance, as well as the Pennsylvania Department of Health’s, and recommending both vitamin A, which can help limit the severity of an infection in children with a deficiency, and a dose of antibodies, which can help prevent an infected mother from transmitting the virus to her child at all. “There’s not a lot of good data on how you treat it,” Goldman said. But, he added, Pennsylvania may soon end up with the country’s largest data set of congenital-measles cases, which could help doctors treat those cases more effectively in future outbreaks. The best way to prevent a congenital-measles infection is, of course, to prevent a mother from getting measles before she gives birth. The best way to do that is with the measles vaccine, which is typically given shortly after a person’s first birthday. One of the few times an adult can’t get vaccinated is, crucially, during pregnancy—just when protection is most necessary. To help shield unvaccinated pregnant women, Roberta Devers argued that the providers who interact with them most often—in many cases, midwives—should be allowed to inoculate the other members of their household. In New York, Governor Kathy Hochul has allowed licensed midwives to administer the measles vaccine as part of a recent disaster declaration responding to the state’s growing outbreak. Pennsylvania, however, does not allow vaccines to be provided by traditional midwives, many of whom study through apprenticeships rather than attending nursing school and are not licensed by the state. Christian Macedonia, a maternal-fetal-medicine physician in Lancaster County, told me that’s for good reason: Providers who have not gone through formal medical training, he said, should not be distributing shots. But he also acknowledged that midwives are “really at the front line” of the congenital-measles crisis. In insular religious communities, such as the Amish one in Lancaster County, which have seen the largest measles outbreaks over the past couple of years, midwives may be the only medical professionals with whom families regularly interact. “We have intimate relationships with these families,” Devers said. “We want to be able to carry the vaccine, because our families started to request it.” Devers knows that many of her patients still distrust the formal health-care system. At a recent postpartum appointment, she talked with a mother who questioned the motives of pop-up vaccination clinics—she was suspicious of the shots being offered for free. As she spoke, the mother cradled her feverish 12-week-old baby, who had measles.

items.title: A Cynical Ploy to Block California’s Wealth Tax
items.description: The most important decision facing California voters this year is not which candidates to support for higher office, but whether to approve a wealth tax on the state’s approximately 250 billionaires. The ballot initiative that would impose the tax has plenty of enemies, among not only the superrich but also the many Californians, including Governor Gavin Newsom, who worry about losing the superrich to other states. But thanks to a deviously cynical electoral maneuver by the measure’s opponents, the people who ultimately doom it might include some of those who vote for it. Proposition 40 was spearheaded by Dave Regan, who leads California’s large and powerful health-care workers’ union, in response to the Medicaid cuts in Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. If approved, the initiative would create a onetime 5 percent tax on all billionaire wealth, and the proceeds—perhaps as much as $100 billion—would be earmarked mostly for state health-care spending. To make sure the superrich don’t flee before they can be taxed, the policy would apply retroactively to anyone who lived in the state at the start of 2026. Predictably, some of the billionaires in question are seeking to defeat the initiative. The Google co-founder Sergey Brin preemptively moved his residence and businesses to Nevada in 2025 and seeded the new political organization Building a Better California with $102 million from his stash. (That might sound like a lot, but the tax would have cost him about $12 billion.) Thanks to the donations of other tech tycoons, the group has raised more than $333 million in total. [ Read: If you tax them, will they leave? ] Plan A is to convince voters that Proposition 40 is unwise via a barrage of TV and social-media ads. In case that doesn’t work, the opponents have come up with Plans B and C: Propositions 41 and 42. These initiatives take advantage of a feature of California law: If two conflicting ballot measures pass in the same election, the one with more votes prevails. On the surface, both look innocuous and unrelated to the wealth tax. Proposition 41 is being pitched as a fiscal-responsibility measure, and Proposition 42 is ostensibly about protecting voters’ retirement savings. But the initiatives are designed to directly conflict with the wealth-tax measure. Proposition 41 would institute audit requirements for new special taxes and void any programs that are exempt from the state’s existing spending limit, which the new wealth tax would be. Proposition 42 would prohibit both retroactive taxes and any taxes on non-real-estate property, each of which describes Proposition 40. This tactic is completely legal, and efforts to change the rules could have unfortunate downstream consequences. For instance, if counterproposals were disallowed, then a group that caught wind of an upcoming initiative could block it simply by being the first to gather enough signatures. Still, the rule can, perversely, lead to antimajoritarian outcomes by preventing proposals supported by more than half of the population from becoming law if another proposal on the ballot happens to, or is designed to, negate it. Propositions 41 and 42 also take advantage of the possibility that voters will not realize that the measures conflict, and will vote yes on more than one of them. They might think that audits are sensible and that spending limits should be observed, or that personal property such as cars and engagement rings and 401(k)s shouldn’t be taxed, and fail to understand that these principles stand in the way of their belief that billionaires ought to pay a wealth tax. Other voters might prefer audits to a wealth tax even though they’d be perfectly fine with both; in that sense, the countermeasure forces them to choose between two policies that could coexist. Still other voters are likely to be overwhelmed or annoyed by having to parse so many measures and decide to oppose all of them: Political scientists have found that the longer the ballot, the more likely people are to vote no. [ Read: The one tax the rich can’t escape ] Historically, Californians are not easily fooled by this type of gamesmanship. But in a close contest, only a small subset of voters needs to fit into the above categories for the countermeasure strategy to work. Imagine that 51 percent of voters want a wealth tax and 49 percent oppose it. If all of those who oppose it vote for Proposition 41, knowing that the measure will negate Proposition 40, and just 3 percent of the electorate votes for both, then Proposition 41 will pass with 52 percent of the vote, nullifying the wealth tax that 51 percent of Californians voted to approve. Polls indicate that this outcome is possible. A September survey by the Public Policy Institute of California had the wealth tax passing 52–46, Proposition 41 passing 51–44, and Proposition 42 passing 54–43, which would result in only Proposition 42 (the one about taxing property) going into effect. (A more recent poll by the same organization showed the wealth tax at only 46 percent support.) A poll from UC Berkeley found that a larger slice of the electorate was undecided about the countermeasures than about Proposition 40, suggesting that some voters don’t realize the measures conflict. At the turn of the 20th century, many western-state legislatures were captured by the owners of local railroad and mining monopolies. Progressives and populists introduced ballot measures as a way to circumvent those plutocrats and return power to the people. But, as the fight over Proposition 40 shows, that works only if voters can withstand plutocrats’ efforts to capture the ballot-measure process too.

items.title: The Real Threat of Election Interference
items.description: I n a speech to the nation in July, Donald Trump said that reports from intelligence agencies showed that American elections were profoundly vulnerable to foreign interference. China had “bought, stolen, or hacked” voter data in 18 states, he said, and he implied that foreign operatives had somehow been able to manipulate actual votes. Reports by the CIA and other agencies that he made public that day did not back up his most extravagant claims. But Trump suggested that a foreign government may have stolen the 2020 election from him, and that it could strike again. Democrats consider that speech a dress rehearsal for next week’s elections. For years, Trump has claimed that foreign governments possess the power to hack electronic voting machines to change the outcome of a race. Election-security experts and lawmakers told me that they expect him to trot out the same claims again if Republicans lose large numbers of seats in the House and Senate. And they’re concerned that he’ll use classified intelligence reports as a pretext for trying to seize ballots or stop vote-counting by the states. “We start with the premise that the president is going to do that,” Representative Jim Himes of Connecticut, the senior Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, told reporters last week. But according to the most recent intelligence that Himes said he had seen about foreign threats to the election, U.S. adversaries haven’t changed votes. “We have never seen an operation to actually interfere,” he said. Years of reporting from intelligence agencies and election-monitoring groups back Himes up. Foreign governments disseminate propaganda and try to undermine confidence in the political process, and they seek to influence policy, sometimes through espionage. But there is a big difference between influence and interference, which experts define as manipulation of an election with the aim of altering the outcome. Top Trump officials have sought to prove that foreign actors worked with Democrats and other “deep state” interests to deny Trump a second term in 2020, only for their theories to come up empty. Former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard went so far as to obtain voting machines from Puerto Rico and test them for evidence of tampering. Her probe found none . One reason voting machines are so secure is that they’re not connected to the internet. “It would be extremely hard for a foreign or outside actor to reach the actual vote,” Lawrence Norden, the vice president of the Elections and Government Program at the Brennan Center, told me. “And we have a paper backup of almost every vote that is cast in the United States at this point,” he added. So even if a hacker managed to flip a vote from one candidate to another on a computer tally, election officials could spot the discrepancy. Norden said that, in his view, foreign governments aren’t the major concern this season. Instead, the dominant source of worry is closer to home. “The new threat in this election is the administration,” Norden said. R eal limits constrain Trump’s ability to interfere in the midterms, even if he tries to do so. The Constitution gives states the power to administer elections, and U.S. law prevents a president from carrying out what many experts consider a nightmare scenario of “nationalizing” the vote. “A mere declaration by the president is not going to be enough legally to justify going in and trying to seize voting machines or ballots,” Richard Pildes, a professor at NYU School of Law, told me. Federal agents would need a warrant to take control of election equipment or ballots, and first they’d need to persuade a judge there was probable cause that a crime had occurred. Any classified intelligence reports might have to be shown to a judge, Pildes said. Even if the government was successful, it cannot legally remove the ballots themselves from state custody, and must rely on copies or images of them, he added. “There’s certainly no power in the executive branch to take over or nationalize the election process,” Pildes said. A White House spokeswoman told me that Trump was focused on prosecuting election crimes, including voter fraud, and on strengthening election infrastructure. The Department of Homeland Security has offered physical security and cybersecurity services to states and localities. “The only ‘concerns’ about election security are being caused by radical Democrats refusing to enact basic election security measures, supported by the majority of Americans, including voter ID and citizenship verification to ensure only Americans are electing America’s leaders,” the spokeswoman, Laruen Biss, said in a statement. “President Trump has done more than any other President to ensure we have free and fair elections.” [ Read: Trump still hasn’t found what he’s looking for ] Should Trump claim that foreign operatives are changing votes, Himes and his counterpart on the Senate Intelligence Committee, Mark Warner of Virginia, told reporters they would call the president’s intelligence advisers and ask for the underlying facts. Himes said that he told CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, “When the president makes that announcement, you will answer your cellphone to give us information about what’s happening.” A spokesperson for Clayton’s office told me that since he was confirmed this summer, he “has made it clear” to the leadership of the House and Senate committees “that he is available to them 24/7 on any issue.” A CIA spokesperson told me, “Director Ratcliffe is responsive to CIA’s Oversight Committees and will continue to be available as appropriate.” Recently, House committee members met with career staff in Clayton’s office who monitor threats to election security. It’s a smaller group these days, after cuts by the administration, Himes said. “But we got a lot of confidence that they are doing their job, that if the president were to demand that they make something up, one way or another, we would learn about that,” he said. T he threat profile from U.S. adversaries this fall is similar to what it’s been before other major U.S. elections in recent years. Russia continues to spread misinformation aimed at undermining public confidence in the political system, voting machines, and Democrats in particular, according to lawmakers and election-security experts. In some cases, Moscow-aligned actors are making deepfake videos with the help of AI to spread false allegations of misconduct . China has focused more on local races and influencing specific policies, often by recruiting agents in the United States. (In May, a former mayor of a Los Angeles suburb pleaded guilty to acting as an illegal foreign agent, primarily by promoting Chinese propaganda.) As for the Iranians, who historically have tried to influence U.S. elections, they appear more focused this year on keeping gas prices high by disrupting traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign influence has been a prominent feature of American politics for a decade now, since Russia used propaganda and selectively leaked emails to divide voters and denigrate Trump’s 2016 opponent, Hillary Clinton. But true interference would be novel, alarming, and contradicted by U.S. intelligence agencies’ best estimates about what foreign adversaries actually hope to achieve. Norden said that both before the election and just after, Russian influence groups are likely to again sow divisions and political discord. One Russian propaganda group in particular, Storm-1516, was active in the 2024 election and could come on the scene again, he said. But peddling misinformation, however corrosive, is not the same thing as flipping votes. Meanwhile, Norden said, the Trump administration has laid the foundations to undermine the public’s confidence in the outcome of the election. That is its own kind of influence operation. [ From the October 2026 issue: The election deniers’ long game ] Intelligence officials seem aware of that particular risk. Back in July, when Trump tried to suggest that China might have had a hand in his loss, the declassified documents that the White House put on its website didn’t substantiate those claims. One CIA document that garnered significant attention from lawmakers and security experts contained a summary of China’s aggressive efforts to exert influence on American politics and economic policy. But it didn’t claim that China had ever interfered and changed votes. If any renewed claims of foreign interference by Trump next Tuesday, or in the days that follow, are to be believed, they will require the sort of evidence that he has so far been unable to supply.

items.title: Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3bn 'complex' security breach
items.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Friday it was working to resolve a “complex attack” that hit around $6.3 billion in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said investigations had “uncovered additional points of breach”, contrary to initial findings that suggested the hack involved a single compromised laptop. “This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance wrote on X. The firm earlier posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages, insisting that “user funds are completely safe” but also saying it would “cover all losses.” The company confirmed on its X account for Latin America that “the total estimated impact is around $6.3 billion.” That is four times the amount impacted in the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: $1.5 billion taken in February last year from the Bybit platform. Binance warned the figure “may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.” It said around $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen. The 2023 Bybit heist was attributed at the time to a group of hackers affiliated with North Korea called TraderTraitor. Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said Thursday it had “high confidence” that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing “robust on and off-chain intelligence.” “Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists,” TRM said. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group – which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for “The Interview,” a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Fund freeze At about 0900 GMT Friday, Binance said it was on track to resume withdrawals in 45 hours, after announcing earlier that all deposits and withdrawals had been “temporarily suspended”. “Deposits remain unaffected,” it said. The company had said on X that initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a “DevOps engineer,” allowing the unauthorised party to access a “service container” and execute unauthorised withdrawal transactions. “We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” it said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete. But it said later that “subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.” Paolo Ardoino, the boss of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs cryptocurrency platform Circle, said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. The US Department of Justice and the FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Crypto prices tumble For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack, except for the stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins. Bitcoin and Ethereum plunged nearly 5 per cent and nearly 6pc respectively on the news. BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10pc. The attack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. Binance has secure asset fund Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. “It’s becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them,” said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company. “My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn’t cover a hack of meaningful size.” World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance’s Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties. Incident adds to string of crypto thefts The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers. Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system. Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident. Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation. In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

items.title: Netanyahu's bloc finishes ahead in Israel election, but well short of majority
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail. The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar. Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”. The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”. Political earthquake The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party alleged on Thursday. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence. Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations. Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority. “He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said. Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”. But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. Qatar called the latest accusations “ridiculous and dangerous”. Kingmakers under pressure Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, told AFP that he is willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government. Netanyahu had tried during the voting to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash, and Likud peddled the accusations throughout Thursday. Police said they arrested three suspects but the election commission called it an isolated local case.
